===== FILE: build.sh =====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds Stremio for PS5 and packages it. Run inside WSL/Ubuntu:
#
#   ./build.sh            install the toolchain if needed, build, package
#
# Output (dist/):
#   PPSA77711.ffpfsc      the whole app as one image file: copy it to
#                         /data/homebrew/ (ShadowMountPlus mounts it). File
#                         permissions are inside it, so they survive any copy
#   PPSA77711/            the same as a folder, for /data/homebrew/PPSA77711
#                         (needs its execute permission restored after copying
#                         with tools that drop it, like PS5 Upload)
#   PPSA77711.zip         the folder, zipped
#
# Stremio is the title's own eboot.bin: one native app, no launcher, no ELF
# loader. See gl/build.sh for how it is compiled and linked.

set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SDK="${PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK:-/opt/ps5-payload-sdk}"

need_apt() {
    local missing=()
    for p in "$@"; do dpkg -s "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p"); done
    if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
        echo ">> installing ${missing[*]}"
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y "${missing[@]}"
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Toolchain: the PS5 payload SDK with prebuilt FFmpeg, curl, libwebp, ...
need_apt clang-18 lld-18 llvm-18 cmake make pkg-config python3 wget zip git ninja-build ccache python3-venv unzip curl

# The payload SDK is a pinned release, verified by SHA-256 before extraction
# (same pin-and-verify pattern as the toolkit's fetch-opengl-sdk.sh).
# To move the pin: export PS5_PAYLOAD_TAG=<tag> and PS5_PAYLOAD_SHA256=<hex>
# together; a mismatched checksum fails the download closed.
PACBREW_TAG="${PS5_PAYLOAD_TAG:-v0.41.1}"
PACBREW_SHA256="${PS5_PAYLOAD_SHA256:-e811bc2e4676c5bb7f80a8fe928d2985dce599996a5ca6b54da3e72699287887}"
if ! [ -e "$SDK/target/user/homebrew/lib/libavformat.a" ]; then
    echo ">> downloading the PS5 payload SDK + libraries ($PACBREW_TAG, about 218 MB)"
    wget -q --show-progress -O /tmp/ps5-payload-dev.tar.gz \
        "https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo/releases/download/$PACBREW_TAG/ps5-payload-dev.tar.gz"
    echo "$PACBREW_SHA256  /tmp/ps5-payload-dev.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check --status || {
        echo "ps5-payload-dev SDK archive checksum mismatch ($PACBREW_TAG)" >&2
        rm -f /tmp/ps5-payload-dev.tar.gz
        exit 2
    }
    sudo tar xf /tmp/ps5-payload-dev.tar.gz -C /
    rm -f /tmp/ps5-payload-dev.tar.gz
fi
export PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK="$SDK"

# The native app's PS5 tooling (converter, signer, libc.prx loader shim) comes
# from ps5-native-app-boilerplate.
BP="${BOILERPLATE_DIR:-$HOME/ps5-native-app-boilerplate}"
BP_COMMIT=f98de73
if ! [ -d "$BP/.git" ]; then
    git clone -q https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate.git "$BP"
fi
git -C "$BP" fetch -q origin && git -C "$BP" checkout -q "$BP_COMMIT"
make -C "$BP" deps >/dev/null
[ -f "$BP/runtime/libc.prx" ] || (cd "$BP" && bash tools/rebuild-libc.sh >/dev/null)
(cd "$BP" && bash tools/build-host-tools.sh >/dev/null)

# The OpenGL SDK (ps5-opengl, a pinned release checked against its SHA-256) is
# downloaded by ps5-homebrew-ui's own script. The toolkit's sources are in
# third_party/hui; the clone is only for that script.
KIT="${KIT_DIR:-$HOME/ps5-homebrew-ui}"
KIT_COMMIT=4bd9425
if ! [ -d "$KIT/.git" ]; then
    git clone -q https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-ui.git "$KIT"
fi
git -C "$KIT" fetch -q origin && git -C "$KIT" checkout -q "$KIT_COMMIT"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BOILERPLATE_DIR="$BP" KIT_DIR="$KIT" bash "$HERE/gl/build.sh" PPSA77711 "Stremio"
echo
echo "Done: copy dist/PPSA77711.ffpfsc to /data/homebrew/"
echo "      (or the folder dist/PPSA77711 to /data/homebrew/PPSA77711)"
ls -la "$HERE/dist" "$HERE/dist/PPSA77711/sce_sys"

constexpr int kPosterW = 480, kPosterH = 720;
// A wallpaper is cut between these widths: never narrower than a 1080p screen (a smaller picture is
// scaled up here, with a good filter, not left to the GPU), and no wider than 2880 (a 4K picture is
// 33 MB on the GPU, 2880 is 19 MB and still sharp on a 4K television).
constexpr int kBackdropMin = 1920, kBackdropMax = 2880;
constexpr int kThumbW = 320;
constexpr int kIconSize = 192;
constexpr int kQrMin = 400;
// A title logo is only ever shrunk: it keeps its own aspect on transparency,
// at most this wide (the hero draws it at 420).
constexpr int kLogoW = 560;

// PNG and JPEG through stb_image; WebP (some addons serve posters as it) through libwebp.
// Hard dimension cap, checked BEFORE any pixel allocation: a hostile file
// claiming gigapixel dimensions would otherwise OOM the art worker and the
// uncaught std::bad_alloc would terminate the process.
constexpr int kDecodeMaxDim = 8000;

bool decode(const std::string &data, std::vector<unsigned char> &px, int &w, int &h)
{
    const unsigned char *bytes = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char *>(data.data());
#ifdef HAVE_WEBP
    if (data.size() >= 12 && std::memcmp(bytes, "RIFF", 4) == 0 && std::memcmp(bytes + 8, "WEBP", 4) == 0)
    {
        if (!WebPGetInfo(bytes, data.size(), &w, &h) || w <= 0 || h <= 0 ||
            w > kDecodeMaxDim || h > kDecodeMaxDim)
            return false;
        uint8_t *out = WebPDecodeRGBA(bytes, data.size(), &w, &h);
        if (!out)
            return false;
        px.assign(out, out + static_cast<std::size_t>(w) * h * 4);
        WebPFree(out);
        return true;
    }
#endif
    int comp = 0;
    int iw = 0, ih = 0, ic = 0;
    if (!stbi_info_from_memory(bytes, static_cast<int>(data.size()), &iw, &ih, &ic) ||
        iw <= 0 || ih <= 0 || iw > kDecodeMaxDim || ih > kDecodeMaxDim)
        return false;
    unsigned char *out = stbi_load_from_memory(bytes, static_cast<int>(data.size()), &w, &h, &comp, 4);
    if (!out)
        return false;
    px.assign(out, out + static_cast<std::size_t>(w) * h * 4);
    stbi_image_free(out);
    return true;
}

// ---- Lanczos-3 resampling (premultiplied, so transparent edges do not fringe) ----

float lanczos3(float x)
{
    x = std::fabs(x);
    if (x < 1e-6f)
        return 1.0f;
    if (x >= 3.0f)
        return 0.0f;
    const float px = 3.14159265f * x;
    return 3.0f * std::sin(px) * std::sin(px / 3.0f) / (px * px);
}

struct Taps
{
    int first = 0;
    std::vector<float> w;
};

std::vector<Taps> make_taps(int n_out, int n_in, float start, float span)
{
    const float scale = span / static_cast<float>(n_out), wide = std::max(1.0f, scale);
    std::vector<Taps> taps(static_cast<std::size_t>(n_out));
    for (int i = 0; i < n_out; ++i)
    {
        const float c = start + (static_cast<float>(i) + 0.5f) * scale - 0.5f;
        int lo = std::max(static_cast<int>(std::floor(c - 3 * wide)) + 1, 0);
        const int hi = std::min(static_cast<int>(std::floor(c + 3 * wide)), n_in - 1);
        Taps &t = taps[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)];
        if (hi < lo)
        {
            lo = std::min(std::max(static_cast<int>(c + 0.5f), 0), n_in - 1);
            t.first = lo;
            t.w.assign(1, 1.0f);
            continue;
        }
        t.first = lo;
        t.w.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(hi - lo + 1));
        float sum = 0;
        for (int k = lo; k <= hi; ++k)
            sum += t.w[static_cast<std::size_t>(k - lo)] = lanczos3((static_cast<float>(k) - c) / wide);
        if (sum <= 0)
        {
            t.w.assign(t.w.size(), 1.0f);
            sum = static_cast<float>(t.w.size());
        }
        for (float &v : t.w)
            v /= sum;
    }
    return taps;
}

// The source rectangle (sx, sy, sw, sh) into dw x dh.
void resample(const unsigned char *src, int src_w, int src_h, float sx, float sy, float sw, float sh,
              unsigned char *dst, int dw, int dh)
{
    const std::vector<Taps> xt = make_taps(dw, src_w, sx, sw), yt = make_taps(dh, src_h, sy, sh);
    int row0 = src_h, row1 = -1;
    for (const Taps &t : yt)
    {
        row0 = std::min(row0, t.first);
        row1 = std::max(row1, t.first + static_cast<int>(t.w.size()) - 1);
    }
    std::vector<float> mid(static_cast<std::size_t>(row1 - row0 + 1) * dw * 4);
    for (int r = row0; r <= row1; ++r)
    {
        const unsigned char *line = src + static_cast<std::size_t>(r) * src_w * 4;
        float *out = &mid[static_cast<std::size_t>(r - row0) * dw * 4];
        for (int x = 0; x < dw; ++x, out += 4)
        {
            const Taps &t = xt[static_cast<std::size_t>(x)];
            float acc[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
            const unsigned char *s = line + static_cast<std::size_t>(t.first) * 4;
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < t.w.size(); ++k, s += 4)
            {
                const float a = static_cast<float>(s[3]) * (1.0f / 255.0f), w = t.w[k];
                acc[0] += s[0] * a * w;
                acc[1] += s[1] * a * w;
                acc[2] += s[2] * a * w;
                acc[3] += a * w;
            }
            std::memcpy(out, acc, sizeof(acc));
        }
    }
    for (int y = 0; y < dh; ++y)
    {
        const Taps &t = yt[static_cast<std::size_t>(y)];
        for (int x = 0; x < dw; ++x)
        {
            float acc[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < t.w.size(); ++k)
            {
                const float *m = &mid[(static_cast<std::size_t>(t.first + static_cast<int>(k) - row0) * dw + x) * 4];
                const float w = t.w[k];
                acc[0] += m[0] * w;
                acc[1] += m[1] * w;
                acc[2] += m[2] * w;
                acc[3] += m[3] * w;
            }
            unsigned char *d = dst + (static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * dw + x) * 4;
            const float a = std::min(std::max(acc[3], 0.0f), 1.0f);
            if (a > 1e-4f)
            {
                const float inv = 1.0f / a;
                for (int c = 0; c < 3; ++c)
                    d[c] = static_cast<unsigned char>(std::min(std::max(acc[c] * inv, 0.0f) + 0.5f, 255.0f));
            }
            else
            {
                d[0] = d[1] = d[2] = 0;
            }
            d[3] = static_cast<unsigned char>(a * 255.0f + 0.5f);
        }
    }
}

// Fills the aspect aw:ah from the middle of the picture, between min_w and max_w wide (with min_w 0 a
// small picture is not scaled up: it is left to the GPU's smooth scaling).
void cover(const std::vector<unsigned char> &src, int w, int h, int aw, int ah, int max_w, std::vector<unsigned char> &out,
           int &ow, int &oh, int min_w = 0)
{
    float sx = 0, sy = 0, sw = static_cast<float>(w), sh = static_cast<float>(h);
    const float target = static_cast<float>(aw) / static_cast<float>(ah), aspect = sw / sh;
    if (aspect > target)
    {
        sw = sh * target;
        sx = (static_cast<float>(w) - sw) * 0.5f;
    }
    else
    {
        sh = sw / target;
        sy = (static_cast<float>(h) - sh) * 0.5f;
    }
    ow = std::max(std::max(1, min_w), std::min(max_w, static_cast<int>(sw)));
    oh = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(std::lround(static_cast<float>(ow) * static_cast<float>(ah) / static_cast<float>(aw))));
    out.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(ow) * oh * 4);
    resample(src.data(), w, h, sx, sy, sw, sh, out.data(), ow, oh);
}

// A picture that was scaled up has lost its edges: a mild unsharp mask (a [1 2 1] blur, taken off
// the picture and a part of it put back) brings them back without a halo.
void sharpen(std::vector<unsigned char> &px, int w, int h, float amount)
{
    std::vector<unsigned char> blur(px.size());
    std::vector<unsigned char> tmp(px.size());
    for (int y = 0; y < h; ++y)
        for (int x = 0; x < w; ++x)
        {
            const int xl = std::max(0, x - 1), xr = std::min(w - 1, x + 1);
            for (int c = 0; c < 3; ++c)
            {
                const std::size_t i = (static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * w + x) * 4 + static_cast<std::size_t>(c);
                tmp[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>((px[(static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * w + xl) * 4 + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] +
                                                      2 * px[i] +
                                                      px[(static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * w + xr) * 4 + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] + 2) /
                                                     4);
            }
        }
    for (int y = 0; y < h; ++y)
    {
        const int yu = std::max(0, y - 1), yd = std::min(h - 1, y + 1);
        for (int x = 0; x < w; ++x)
            for (int c = 0; c < 3; ++c)
            {
                const std::size_t i = (static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * w + x) * 4 + static_cast<std::size_t>(c);
                blur[i] = static_cast<unsigned char>((tmp[(static_cast<std::size_t>(yu) * w + x) * 4 + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] +
                                                       2 * tmp[i] +
                                                       tmp[(static_cast<std::size_t>(yd) * w + x) * 4 + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] + 2) /
                                                      4);
            }
    }
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < px.size(); i += 4)
        for (int c = 0; c < 3; ++c)
        {
            const float v = static_cast<float>(px[i + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)]);
            const float b = static_cast<float>(blur[i + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)]);
            px[i + static_cast<std::size_t>(c)] = static_cast<unsigned char>(std::clamp(v + amount * (v - b), 0.0f, 255.0f));
        }
}

// The whole picture inside a square on transparency.
void fit_square(const std::vector<unsigned char> &src, int w, int h, int size, std::vector<unsigned char> &out)
{
    const float aspect = static_cast<float>(w) / static_cast<float>(h);
    int fw = size, fh = size;
    if (aspect > 1.0f)
        fh = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(std::lround(static_cast<float>(size) / aspect)));
    else
        fw = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(std::lround(static_cast<float>(size) * aspect)));
    std::vector<unsigned char> fitted(static_cast<std::size_t>(fw) * fh * 4);
    resample(src.data(), w, h, 0, 0, static_cast<float>(w), static_cast<float>(h), fitted.data(), fw, fh);
    out.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(size) * size * 4, 0);
    const int ox = (size - fw) / 2, oy = (size - fh) / 2;
    for (int y = 0; y < fh; ++y)
        std::memcpy(&out[(static_cast<std::size_t>(y + oy) * size + ox) * 4], &fitted[static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * fw * 4],
                    static_cast<std::size_t>(fw) * 4);
}

// Shrink to at most max_w wide, keeping the aspect; smaller pictures are left
// alone. No crop, no letterbox: the alpha stays exactly the artwork's own.
void fit_width(const std::vector<unsigned char> &src, int w, int h, int max_w, std::vector<unsigned char> &out,
              int &ow, int &oh)
{
    const float scale = std::min(1.0f, static_cast<float>(max_w) / static_cast<float>(w));
    ow = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(std::lround(static_cast<float>(w) * scale)));
    oh = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(std::lround(static_cast<float>(h) * scale)));
    out.assign(static_cast<std::size_t>(ow) * oh * 4, 0);
    resample(src.data(), w, h, 0, 0, static_cast<float>(w), static_cast<float>(h), out.data(), ow, oh);
}

void to_string_sink(void *context, void *data, int size)
{
    static_cast<std::string *>(context)->append(static_cast<const char *>(data), static_cast<std::size_t>(size));
}

// How far apart two pictures are (0..255): the average difference of their brightness on a 32 x 18 grid.
float luma_distance(const std::vector<unsigned char> &a, int aw, int ah, const std::vector<unsigned char> &b, int bw, int bh)
{
    const auto luma = [](const std::vector<unsigned char> &p, int w, int h, int x, int y) {
        const std::size_t i = (static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * w + x) * 4;
        (void)h;
        return (p[i] * 299 + p[i + 1] * 587 + p[i + 2] * 114) / 1000;
    };
    long sum = 0;
    for (int gy = 0; gy < 18; ++gy)
        for (int gx = 0; gx < 32; ++gx)
        {
            const float fx = (static_cast<float>(gx) + 0.5f) / 32.0f, fy = (static_cast<float>(gy) + 0.5f) / 18.0f;
            sum += std::abs(luma(a, aw, ah, static_cast<int>(fx * aw), static_cast<int>(fy * ah)) -
                            luma(b, bw, bh, static_cast<int>(fx * bw), static_cast<int>(fy * bh)));
        }
    return static_cast<float>(sum) / (32.0f * 18.0f);
}

// The image host keeps a bigger copy of many wallpapers: the "medium" one is often 1280 wide, the
// "big" one 3840. Not always the same picture, though: for some titles "big" is other artwork (a poster-like
// still with the name in it), so it is only taken when it is the picture we already have, bigger.
void use_bigger_copy(const std::string &url, std::vector<unsigned char> &src, int &w, int &h)
{
    static const std::string kMedium = "/background/medium/";
    const std::size_t at = url.find(kMedium);
    if (at == std::string::npos || w >= 2880)
        return;
    std::string big_url = url;
    big_url.replace(at, kMedium.size(), "/background/big/");
    const HttpResponse r = http_get(big_url, 40);
    if (!r.ok())
        return;
    std::vector<unsigned char> big;
    int bw = 0, bh = 0;
    if (!decode(r.body, big, bw, bh) || bw <= w || bh <= 0)
        return;
    if (luma_distance(src, w, h, big, bw, bh) < 4.0f)
    {
        src.swap(big);
        w = bw;
        h = bh;
    }
}

bool opaque_kind(ArtKind kind)
{
    return kind == ArtKind::poster || kind == ArtKind::backdrop || kind == ArtKind::thumb;
}

const char *suffix(ArtKind kind)
{
    switch (kind)
    {
    case ArtKind::poster:
        return "p";
    case ArtKind::backdrop:
        return "b2"; // (b: the first cuts, 1920 wide at most)
    case ArtKind::thumb:
        return "t";
    case ArtKind::icon:
        return "i";
    case ArtKind::logo:
        return "l";
    case ArtKind::qr:
        return "q";
    }
    return "x";
}

} // namespace

bool TexCache::init(const std::string &dir, hui::gfx::Renderer *renderer, int workers)
{
    dir_ = dir;
    renderer_ = renderer;
    make_dirs(dir_);
    stopping_ = false;
    for (int i = 0; i < workers; ++i)
        threads_.emplace_back([this] { worker(); });
    return true;
}

void TexCache::shutdown()
{
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        stopping_ = true;
        queue_.clear();
    }
    cv_.notify_all();
    for (std::thread &t : threads_)
        t.join();
    threads_.clear();
}

std::string TexCache::key_for(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind) const
{
    char name[64];
    std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "/%016llx%s.%s", static_cast<unsigned long long>(fnv1a(url)), suffix(kind),
                  opaque_kind(kind) ? "jpg" : "png");
    return dir_ + name;
}

std::uint32_t TexCache::get(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind)
{
    if (url.empty() || (!starts_with(url, "http://") && !starts_with(url, "https://")))
        return 0;
    const std::string key = key_for(url, kind);
    Entry &e = entries_[key];
    e.used_sec = now_seconds();
    if (e.id != 0)
        return e.id;
    if (e.pending || e.failed)
        return 0;
    e.pending = true;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        queue_.push_back(Job{url, key, kind, epoch_.load()});
    }
    cv_.notify_one();
    return 0;
}

std::uint32_t TexCache::peek(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind) const
{
    const auto it = entries_.find(key_for(url, kind));
    return it == entries_.end() ? 0 : it->second.id;
}

bool TexCache::dims(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind, int *w, int *h) const
{
    const auto it = entries_.find(key_for(url, kind));
    if (it == entries_.end() || it->second.id == 0 || it->second.tw <= 0 || it->second.th <= 0)
        return false;
    *w = it->second.tw;
    *h = it->second.th;
    return true;
}

bool TexCache::pump(int max_uploads)
{
    // The disk cache is capped at 2 GB, oldest first; the scan runs at most
    // once a minute and only after a worker actually wrote something.
    if (disk_written_.load())
    {
        const double now = now_seconds();
        if (now - last_disk_prune_ > 60.0)
        {
            last_disk_prune_ = now;
            disk_written_.store(false);
            prune_disk();
        }
    }
    std::vector<Ready> batch;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        // Per-frame upload budget: at most one large texture (> 1 MB, e.g. a
        // backdrop/poster) per frame, plus small ones up to a modest byte cap.
        // A burst of ready backdrops used to stall the render thread for a
        // whole frame of back-to-back glTexImage2D uploads.
        static const std::size_t kLargeBytes = 1u << 20;
        static const std::size_t kSmallCap = 2u << 20;
        bool large_taken = false;
        std::size_t small_bytes = 0;
        std::size_t taken = 0;
        for (auto it = ready_.begin(); it != ready_.end() && taken < static_cast<std::size_t>(max_uploads);)
        {
            const std::size_t bytes = it->pixels.size();
            const bool large = bytes > kLargeBytes;
            if (!it->pixels.empty() && (large ? large_taken : small_bytes + bytes > kSmallCap))
            {
                ++it; // over budget this frame: stays queued for the next one
                continue;
            }
            if (large)
                large_taken = true;
            else
                small_bytes += bytes;
            batch.push_back(std::move(*it));
            it = ready_.erase(it);
            ++taken;
        }
    }
    for (Ready &r : batch)
    {
        Entry &e = entries_[r.key];
        e.pending = false;
        if (r.dropped)
            continue; // stale: may be asked for again
        if (r.pixels.empty())
        {
            e.failed = true;
            continue;
        }
        e.id = renderer_->batch().create_texture(r.w, r.h, r.pixels.data());
        e.bytes = r.pixels.size();
        e.used_sec = now_seconds();
        e.tw = r.w;
        e.th = r.h;
        bytes_ += e.bytes;
    }
    return !batch.empty();
}

bool TexCache::trim(std::size_t budget)
{
    if (bytes_ <= budget)
        return false;
    bool deleted = false;
    // Wall-clock grace: a texture unused for 120 s may go; scrolling back
    // within that window finds it still on the GPU (no re-decode pop-in).
    // The 640 MB budget below is still the hard cap.
    const double now = now_seconds();
    std::vector<std::map<std::string, Entry>::iterator> loaded;
    for (auto it = entries_.begin(); it != entries_.end(); ++it)
        if (it->second.id != 0 && now - it->second.used_sec > 120.0)
            loaded.push_back(it);
    std::sort(loaded.begin(), loaded.end(),
              [](const auto &a, const auto &b) { return a->second.used_sec < b->second.used_sec; });
    for (auto &it : loaded)
    {
        if (bytes_ <= budget)
            break;
        const GLuint id = it->second.id;
        glDeleteTextures(1, &id);
        bytes_ -= it->second.bytes;
        entries_.erase(it);
        deleted = true;
    }
    return deleted;
}

void TexCache::prune_disk()
{
    struct File
    {
        std::string path;
        std::uint64_t mtime = 0;
        std::uint64_t size = 0;
    };
    std::vector<File> files;
    std::uint64_t total = 0;
    if (DIR *d = opendir(dir_.c_str()))
    {
        while (dirent *e = readdir(d))
        {
            if (e->d_name[0] == '.')
                continue;
            const std::string name = e->d_name;
            // Skip in-flight temp files: write_file() is still filling them.
            if (name.size() > 4 && name.compare(name.size() - 4, 4, ".tmp") == 0)
                continue;
            const std::string p = dir_ + "/" + name;
            struct stat st;
            if (stat(p.c_str(), &st) != 0 || !S_ISREG(st.st_mode))
                continue;
            files.push_back({p, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(st.st_mtime), static_cast<std::uint64_t>(st.st_size)});
            total += static_cast<std::uint64_t>(st.st_size);
        }
        closedir(d);
    }
    static const std::uint64_t kDiskCap = 2ull << 30;
    if (total <= kDiskCap)
        return;
    std::sort(files.begin(), files.end(),
              [](const File &a, const File &b) { return a.mtime < b.mtime; });
    for (const File &f : files)
    {
        if (total <= kDiskCap)
            break;
        if (unlink(f.path.c_str()) == 0)
            total -= f.size;
    }
    dlog("art: disk cache pruned to %llu MB", static_cast<unsigned long long>(total >> 20));
}

void TexCache::worker()
{
    for (;;)
    {
        Job job;
        {
            std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
            cv_.wait(lock, [this] { return stopping_ || !queue_.empty(); });
            if (stopping_)
                return;
            job = queue_.back();
            queue_.pop_back();
        }
        Ready r;
        r.key = job.key;
        try
        {
            if (job.epoch != epoch_.load())
            {
                // The cursor moved past this one while it waited: drop it before
                // the download. The dropped marker clears pending without marking
                // it failed, so asking again later still works.
                r.dropped = true;
            }
            else if (!make(job, &r))
                r.pixels.clear();
        }
        catch (const std::bad_alloc &)
        {
            // A hostile image slipped past the caps: don't let the worker
            // thread die (an uncaught exception here would std::terminate).
            dlog("art: out of memory decoding %s", job.url.c_str());
            r.pixels.clear();
        }
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        ready_.push_back(std::move(r));
    }
}

bool TexCache::make(const Job &job, Ready *out)
{
    std::string data;
    if (read_file(job.key, data) && decode(data, out->pixels, out->w, out->h))
        return true; // already cut: use as it is

    const HttpResponse r = http_get(job.url, 30);
    if (!r.ok())
    {
        dlog("art: %s: %s", job.url.c_str(), r.describe().c_str());
        return false;
    }
    std::vector<unsigned char> src;
    int w = 0, h = 0;
    if (!decode(r.body, src, w, h) || w <= 0 || h <= 0)
    {
        dlog("art: cannot decode %s", job.url.c_str());
        return false;
    }
    if (job.kind == ArtKind::backdrop)
        use_bigger_copy(job.url, src, w, h);

    std::vector<unsigned char> px;
    int ow = 0, oh = 0;
    switch (job.kind)
    {
    case ArtKind::poster:
        cover(src, w, h, 2, 3, kPosterW, px, ow, oh);
        break;
    case ArtKind::backdrop:
    {
        cover(src, w, h, 16, 9, kBackdropMax, px, ow, oh, kBackdropMin);
        // Was it made bigger? Then its edges need a little help.
        const float cropped_w = std::min(static_cast<float>(w), static_cast<float>(h) * 16.0f / 9.0f);
        if (static_cast<float>(ow) > cropped_w * 1.1f)
            sharpen(px, ow, oh, 0.45f);
        break;
    }
    case ArtKind::thumb:
        cover(src, w, h, 16, 9, kThumbW, px, ow, oh);
        break;
    case ArtKind::icon:
        fit_square(src, w, h, kIconSize, px);
        ow = oh = kIconSize;
        break;
    case ArtKind::logo:
        fit_width(src, w, h, kLogoW, px, ow, oh);
        break;
    case ArtKind::qr:
    {
        const int step = std::max(1, (kQrMin + w - 1) / w);
        ow = w * step;
        oh = h * step;
        px.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(ow) * oh * 4);
        for (int y = 0; y < oh; ++y)
            for (int x = 0; x < ow; ++x)
                std::memcpy(&px[(static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * ow + x) * 4], &src[(static_cast<std::size_t>(y / step) * w + x / step) * 4], 4);
        break;
    }
    }

    std::string file;
    if (opaque_kind(job.kind))
        stbi_write_jpg_to_func(to_string_sink, &file, ow, oh, 4, px.data(), job.kind == ArtKind::backdrop ? 93 : 90);
    else
        stbi_write_png_to_func(to_string_sink, &file, ow, oh, 4, px.data(), ow * 4);
    if (!file.empty())
    {
        write_file(job.key, file);
        disk_written_.store(true);
    }
    out->pixels = std::move(px);
    out->w = ow;
    out->h = oh;
    return true;
}

} // namespace sx


===== FILE: gl/art.hpp =====
// Artwork as GL textures: downloaded (or read from the disk cache), cut to the
// shape it is drawn in, decoded on worker threads and uploaded on the thread
// that owns the GL context.
//
// Every picture is stored once on disk already cut and scaled (a JPEG for
// opaque pictures, a PNG where transparency matters), so the second visit costs
// a small decode instead of a download. The GPU draws rounded corners itself, so
// nothing is pre-rounded and one file serves every screen size.

#pragma once

#include "gfx/renderer.hpp"

#include <atomic>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstdint>
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

namespace sx
{

enum class ArtKind
{
    poster,   // 2:3, up to 480x720 (cards)
    backdrop, // 16:9, up to 1920x1080 (the hero, a title's page)
    thumb,    // 16:9, up to 320x180 (episodes)
    icon,     // 192x192, fitted on transparency (addon logos)
    logo,     // transparent title art, up to 560 wide, aspect kept (the hero)
    qr,       // scaled by whole steps to at least 400 px, never smoothed
};

class TexCache
{
  public:
    ~TexCache()
    {
        shutdown();
    }

    // `dir` is where the processed pictures are kept.
    bool init(const std::string &dir, hui::gfx::Renderer *renderer, int workers);
    void shutdown();

    // The texture, or 0 while it is still coming (the download is queued, and
    // newer requests are served first). Call from the GL thread only.
    std::uint32_t get(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind);
    // The texture if it is already on the GPU, without asking for it.
    std::uint32_t peek(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind) const;
    // The decoded pixel dimensions of a cached texture; false when unknown.
    // Lets callers draw artwork at its own aspect (title logos must not stretch).
    bool dims(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind, int *w, int *h) const;

    // Once per frame on the GL thread: uploads up to max_uploads decoded
    // pictures. Returns true if any arrived.
    bool pump(int max_uploads);
    // Deletes the least recently asked-for textures until the cache is under
    // `budget` bytes. Textures asked for in the last 120 seconds stay.
    // Returns true if it deleted any: the owners of those ids must look again.
    bool trim(std::size_t budget);
    // The cursor moved on: queued jobs from the old position are stale and
    // the workers drop them before downloading. Call from the GL thread.
    void bump_epoch() { epoch_.fetch_add(1); }
    std::size_t bytes() const
    {
        return bytes_;
    }

  private:
    struct Entry
    {
        std::uint32_t id = 0;
        std::size_t bytes = 0;
        double used_sec = 0.0; // last asked-for, wall clock (eviction grace)
        bool pending = false;
        bool failed = false;
        int tw = 0; // decoded pixel width, for aspect-kept drawing
        int th = 0; // decoded pixel height
    };
    struct Job
    {
        std::string url;
        std::string key;
        ArtKind kind;
        std::uint64_t epoch = 0; // the cursor epoch that queued it
    };
    struct Ready
    {
        std::string key;
        int w = 0;
        int h = 0;
        std::vector<unsigned char> pixels; // empty when it failed
        bool dropped = false; // stale epoch: clear pending, not failed
    };

    std::string key_for(const std::string &url, ArtKind kind) const;
    void worker();
    bool make(const Job &job, Ready *out);
    // LRU-by-mtime prune of the disk cache (GL thread only).
    void prune_disk();

    std::string dir_;
    hui::gfx::Renderer *renderer_ = nullptr;
    std::map<std::string, Entry> entries_; // GL thread only
    std::size_t bytes_ = 0;

    std::mutex mutex_;
    std::condition_variable cv_;
    std::vector<Job> queue_; // newest last: served first
    std::vector<Ready> ready_;
    std::vector<std::thread> threads_;
    bool stopping_ = false;
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> epoch_{0}; // bumped when the cursor moves on
    std::atomic<bool> disk_written_{false}; // a worker saved a file: prune may be due
    double last_disk_prune_ = 0.0;          // GL thread only
};

} // namespace sx

===== FILE: gl/gpu_convert.cpp =====
// GPU YUV->RGB conversion for the video picture. See gpu_convert.hpp.

#include "gpu_convert.hpp"

#include <cmath>

#include <GL/glcorearb.h>

#include "gfx/gl_program.hpp"
#include "util.h"
#include "yuv_convert.h"

namespace {

// Full-screen triangle from the vertex id alone; no vertex buffers.
const char* kVert = R"(
out vec2 v_uv;
void main() {
	vec2 p = vec2(float((gl_VertexID << 1) & 2), float(gl_VertexID & 2));
	v_uv = p;
	gl_Position = vec4(p * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}
)";

// The conversion of src/yuv_convert.cpp in float: studio-range YUV to RGB
// with the BT.601/BT.709 matrix, or HDR10 (BT.2020, PQ, Hable tone mapping
// on the brightest channel, BT.2020->BT.709, BT.709 OETF).
const char* kFrag = R"(
uniform sampler2D y_tex;
uniform sampler2D c_tex;  // planar U, or interleaved UV
uniform sampler2D v_tex;  // planar V (ignored when u_interleaved != 0)
uniform sampler2D pq_tex; // 1024x1: PQ code -> light, units of 100 nits
uniform int u_colors;     // 0 = BT.601, 1 = BT.709, 2 = HDR10 (PQ), 3 = HLG, 4 = DV P5
uniform int u_interleaved;
uniform float u_peak;     // sample scale to the 10-bit domain: 1020 or 65535
uniform float u_shift_div; // 1, or 64 for high-aligned 10-bit samples
in vec2 v_uv;
out vec4 o_color;

float hable(float x) {
	const float a = 0.15, b = 0.50, c = 0.10, d = 0.20, e = 0.02, f = 0.30;
	return (x * (a * x + c * b) + d * e) / (x * (a * x + b) + d * f) - e / f;
}
float bt709_oetf(float l) {
	l = clamp(l, 0.0, 1.0);
	return l < 0.018 ? 4.5 * l : 1.099 * pow(l, 0.45) - 0.099;
}
float pq_lut(float e) {
	// The CPU path's 1024-entry table, indexed exactly as it does:
	// code = clamp(int(e * 1023 + 0.5), 0, 1023).
	float j = floor(clamp(e, 0.0, 1.0) * 1023.0 + 0.5);
	return texture(pq_tex, vec2((j + 0.5) / 1024.0, 0.5)).r;
}
float hlg_inv(float e) {
	// BT.2100 inverse HLG OETF: HLG code value to scene light E, nominal
	// 1000-nit peak. (The forward OETF maps the other way and must not be
	// used here.)
	e = clamp(e, 0.0, 1.0);
	return e <= 0.5 ? e * e / 3.0 : (exp((e - 0.55991073) / 0.17883277) + 0.28466892) / 12.0;
}
void main() {
	float y10 = texture(y_tex, v_uv).r * u_peak / u_shift_div;
	float u10, v10;
	if (u_interleaved != 0) {
		vec2 cuv = texture(c_tex, v_uv).rg;
		u10 = cuv.r * u_peak / u_shift_div;
		v10 = cuv.g * u_peak / u_shift_div;
	} else {
		u10 = texture(c_tex, v_uv).r * u_peak / u_shift_div;
		v10 = texture(v_tex, v_uv).r * u_peak / u_shift_div;
	}
	vec3 rgb;
	if (u_colors == 2) {
		float y = (y10 - 64.0) / 876.0;
		float cb = (u10 - 512.0) / 896.0;
		float cr = (v10 - 512.0) / 896.0;
		vec3 pq = vec3(pq_lut(y + 1.4746 * cr), pq_lut(y - 0.16455 * cb - 0.57135 * cr),
		             pq_lut(y + 1.8814 * cb))
		          * 2.5;
		vec3 t;
		t.r = 1.6605 * pq.r - 0.5876 * pq.g - 0.0728 * pq.b;
		t.g = -0.1246 * pq.r + 1.1329 * pq.g - 0.0083 * pq.b;
		t.b = -0.0182 * pq.r - 0.1006 * pq.g + 1.1187 * pq.b;
		float sig = max(max(t.r, t.g), max(t.b, 1e-6));
		t *= hable(sig) / hable(10.0) / sig;
		rgb = vec3(bt709_oetf(t.r), bt709_oetf(t.g), bt709_oetf(t.b));
	} else if (u_colors == 3) {
		// HLG (BT.2100): same pipeline as HDR10, but the inverse HLG OETF
		// instead of the PQ table. hlg_inv gives scene light E with a
		// nominal 1000-nit peak, so E * 10 is light in units of 100 nits,
		// the same units pq_lut produces. No 2.5x gain: HLG's 50% knee
		// lands at ~50% SDR through Hable, which is HLG's SDR
		// backward-compatibility design.
		float y = (y10 - 64.0) / 876.0;
		float cb = (u10 - 512.0) / 896.0;
		float cr = (v10 - 512.0) / 896.0;
		vec3 hlg = vec3(hlg_inv(y + 1.4746 * cr), hlg_inv(y - 0.16455 * cb - 0.57135 * cr),
		             hlg_inv(y + 1.8814 * cb))
		          * 10.0;
		vec3 t;
		t.r = 1.6605 * hlg.r - 0.5876 * hlg.g - 0.0728 * hlg.b;
		t.g = -0.1246 * hlg.r + 1.1329 * hlg.g - 0.0083 * hlg.b;
		t.b = -0.0182 * hlg.r - 0.1006 * hlg.g + 1.1187 * hlg.b;
		float sig = max(max(t.r, t.g), max(t.b, 1e-6));
		t *= hable(sig) / hable(10.0) / sig;
		rgb = vec3(bt709_oetf(t.r), bt709_oetf(t.g), bt709_oetf(t.b));
	} else if (u_colors == 4) {
		// Dolby Vision Profile 5: the planes hold reshaped IPT-PQ-c2, not
		// YCbCr (P5 has no HDR10 base layer). Reshape to HDR10 on the GPU,
		// then the frame flows through the HDR10 tone-mapping tail below.
		//
		// v1: identity reshaping (no per-frame RPU curves) with Dolby's
		// reference matrices (FFmpeg's ff_dovi_color_default, the defaults
		// EVO Player uses when the RPU carries none). P5 is full-range, so
		// the 10-bit codes normalize by /1023, not the studio-range
		// formula the HDR10/HLG branches use.
		//
		// Pipeline (EVO/libplacebo order): raw signal -> per-component
		// reshape (identity here) -> YCC matrix -> LMS' -> PQ EOTF ->
		// linear LMS -> LMS->BT.2020 RGB -> HDR10 tail.
		vec3 ipt = vec3(y10, u10, v10) / 1023.0;
		// YCC->LMS' (ff_dovi_color_default ycc_to_rgb_matrix), with the
		// neutral offsets {0, 0.5, 0.5} that P5 RPUs carry in the wild.
		vec3 lmsp;
		lmsp.r = 1.16882324 * (ipt.r - 0.0) + 0.0 * (ipt.g - 0.5) + 1.79956055 * (ipt.b - 0.5);
		lmsp.g = 1.16882324 * (ipt.r - 0.0) + 0.21411133 * (ipt.g - 0.5) + 0.53503418 * (ipt.b - 0.5);
		lmsp.b = 1.16882324 * (ipt.r - 0.0) + 2.12060547 * (ipt.g - 0.5) + 0.0 * (ipt.b - 0.5);
		// PQ EOTF -> linear LMS, in units of 100 nits like pq_lut.
		vec3 lms = vec3(pq_lut(lmsp.r), pq_lut(lmsp.g), pq_lut(lmsp.b));
		// RGB->LMS (ff_dovi_color_default rgb_to_lms_matrix)...
		vec3 tmp;
		tmp.r = 0.35675049 * lms.r + 0.59216309 * lms.g + 0.05108643 * lms.b;
		tmp.g = 0.15673828 * lms.r + 0.74804688 * lms.g + 0.09527588 * lms.b;
		tmp.b = 0.0 * lms.r + 0.04144287 * lms.g + 0.95855713 * lms.b;
		// ...then HPE LMS -> linear BT.2020 RGB (libplacebo dovi_lms2rgb,
		// the same matrix EVO Player uses).
		vec3 dv;
		dv.r = 3.06441879 * tmp.r - 2.16597676 * tmp.g + 0.10155818 * tmp.b;
		dv.g = -0.65612108 * tmp.r + 1.78554118 * tmp.g - 0.12943749 * tmp.b;
		dv.b = 0.01736321 * tmp.r - 0.04725154 * tmp.g + 1.03004253 * tmp.b;
		// Now ordinary HDR10: the same 2.5x gain, BT.2020->BT.709,
		// Hable(10.0), BT.709 OETF as the HDR10 branch.
		dv *= 2.5;
		vec3 t;
		t.r = 1.6605 * dv.r - 0.5876 * dv.g - 0.0728 * dv.b;
		t.g = -0.1246 * dv.r + 1.1329 * dv.g - 0.0083 * dv.b;
		t.b = -0.0182 * dv.r - 0.1006 * dv.g + 1.1187 * dv.b;
		float sig = max(max(t.r, t.g), max(t.b, 1e-6));
		t *= hable(sig) / hable(10.0) / sig;
		rgb = vec3(bt709_oetf(t.r), bt709_oetf(t.g), bt709_oetf(t.b));
	} else {
		float y8 = y10 * 0.25;
		float u8 = u10 * 0.25 - 128.0;
		float v8 = v10 * 0.25 - 128.0;
		float c = 298.0 * (y8 - 16.0) + 128.0;
		vec4 m = u_colors == 0 ? vec4(409.0, 100.0, 208.0, 516.0)   // BT.601
		                       : vec4(459.0, 55.0, 136.0, 541.0);  // BT.709
		// /256 is the integer >>8 of put_sdr(); /255 puts it in 0..1.
		rgb = vec3(c + m.x * v8, c - m.y * u8 - m.z * v8, c + m.w * u8) / (256.0 * 255.0);
	}
	o_color = vec4(clamp(rgb, 0.0, 1.0), 1.0);
}
)";

// PQ code value (0..1) to light, units of 100 nits: src/yuv_convert.cpp.
float pq_eotf(float e) {
	const float m1 = 0.1593017578125f, m2 = 78.84375f, c1 = 0.8359375f, c2 = 18.8515625f,
	            c3 = 18.6875f;
	float p = std::pow(std::max(e, 0.0f), 1.0f / m2);
	float l = std::pow(std::max(p - c1, 0.0f) / (c2 - c3 * p), 1.0f / m1);
	return l * 100.0f;
}

void tex_params() {
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
}

}  // namespace

bool GpuYuv::gl_ok(const char* what) {
	GLenum e = glGetError();
	if (e != GL_NO_ERROR) {
		if (!logged_fail_) {
			logged_fail_ = true;
			dlog("gpu: %s: GL error 0x%x; falling back to the CPU path", what, unsigned(e));
		}
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

bool GpuYuv::ensure() {
	if (program_) return true;
	if (logged_fail_) return false;  // tried once; don't spam the log
	auto fail = [&] {
		if (program_) glDeleteProgram(program_);
		program_ = 0;
		logged_fail_ = true;
		dlog("gpu: YUV shaders unavailable; staying on the CPU path");
		return false;
	};
	program_ = hui::gfx::build_program("yuv", kVert, kFrag);
	if (!program_) return fail();  // build_program logs the info log itself
	u_y_tex_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "y_tex");
	u_c_tex_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "c_tex");
	u_v_tex_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "v_tex");
	u_pq_tex_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "pq_tex");
	u_colors_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "u_colors");
	u_interleaved_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "u_interleaved");
	u_peak_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "u_peak");
	u_shift_div_ = glGetUniformLocation(program_, "u_shift_div");
	if (u_y_tex_ < 0 || u_c_tex_ < 0 || u_v_tex_ < 0 || u_pq_tex_ < 0 || u_colors_ < 0 ||
	    u_interleaved_ < 0 || u_peak_ < 0 || u_shift_div_ < 0)
		return fail();
	glGenVertexArrays(1, &vao_);
	glGenFramebuffers(1, &fbo_);
	// The PQ curve as a 1D lookup, like the CPU path's 1024-entry table.
	float pq[1024];
	for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++) pq[i] = pq_eotf(i / 1023.0f);
	glGenTextures(1, &tex_pq_);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tex_pq_);
	glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_R32F, 1024, 1, 0, GL_RED, GL_FLOAT, pq);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
	if (!gl_ok("pq lut")) return fail();
	dlog("gpu: YUV conversion ready");
	return true;
}

bool GpuYuv::upload_planes(const Player::Picture& pic) {
	const YuvPicture& p = pic.planes;
	// Never pass a null pointer to glTexSubImage2D: bail out and let the
	// caller fall back to the CPU conversion instead.
	if (!p.y || !p.u || (!p.interleaved && !p.v)) return false;
	const int cw = p.width / 2, ch = p.height / 2;
	const bool wide = p.wide;
	const GLenum type = wide ? GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT : GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE;
	if (!tex_y_ || py_w_ != p.width || py_h_ != p.height || pc_w_ != cw || pc_h_ != ch || wide_ != wide ||
	    interleaved_ != p.interleaved) {
		for (GLuint t : {tex_y_, tex_c_, tex_v_})
			if (t) glDeleteTextures(1, &t);
		tex_y_ = tex_c_ = tex_v_ = 0;
		auto alloc = [&](GLuint& t, int w, int h, GLenum internal, GLenum format) {
			glGenTextures(1, &t);
			glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, t);
			glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, internal, w, h, 0, format, type, nullptr);
			tex_params();
		};
		if (wide) {
			alloc(tex_y_, p.width, p.height, GL_R16, GL_RED);
			if (p.interleaved) alloc(tex_c_, cw, ch, GL_RG16, GL_RG);
			else {
				alloc(tex_c_, cw, ch, GL_R16, GL_RED);
				alloc(tex_v_, cw, ch, GL_R16, GL_RED);
			}
		} else {
			alloc(tex_y_, p.width, p.height, GL_R8, GL_RED);
			if (p.interleaved) alloc(tex_c_, cw, ch, GL_RG8, GL_RG);
			else {
				alloc(tex_c_, cw, ch, GL_R8, GL_RED);
				alloc(tex_v_, cw, ch, GL_R8, GL_RED);
			}
		}
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
		if (!gl_ok("plane alloc")) return false;
		py_w_ = p.width;
		py_h_ = p.height;
		pc_w_ = cw;
		pc_h_ = ch;
		wide_ = wide;
		interleaved_ = p.interleaved;
	}
	// The player packs the planes tightly, so one row length works for all.
	glPixelStorei(GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 1);
	auto upload = [&](GLuint t, int w, int h, GLenum format, const uint8_t* data) {
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, t);
		glTexSubImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, 0, 0, w, h, format, type, data);
	};
	upload(tex_y_, p.width, p.height, GL_RED, p.y);
	if (p.interleaved) upload(tex_c_, cw, ch, GL_RG, p.u);
	else {
		upload(tex_c_, cw, ch, GL_RED, p.u);
		upload(tex_v_, cw, ch, GL_RED, p.v);
	}
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
	bool ok = gl_ok("plane upload");
	glPixelStorei(GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
	return ok;
}

bool GpuYuv::render(const Player::Picture& pic, std::uint32_t& target, int& tw, int& th) {
	if (!ready() || !pic.yuv) return false;
	// Render at source resolution, not the output box. The upscaler (or the
	// shell's draw) handles scaling to display size. This lets the upscaler
	// engagement check (video_w < display_w) work correctly.
	const int sw = pic.src_w > 0 ? pic.src_w : pic.w;
	const int sh = pic.src_h > 0 ? pic.src_h : pic.h;
	if (sw <= 0 || sh <= 0) return false;
	if (!upload_planes(pic)) return false;
	GLuint tgt = target;
	if (!tgt || tw != sw || th != sh) {
		if (tgt) glDeleteTextures(1, &tgt);
		glGenTextures(1, &tgt);
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tgt);
		glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA8, sw, sh, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, nullptr);
		tex_params();
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
		if (!gl_ok("target alloc")) {
			if (tgt) glDeleteTextures(1, &tgt);
			return false;
		}
		tw = sw;
		th = sh;
		fbo_checked_ = false;  // new target texture: re-verify completeness once
	}
	GLint vp[4];
	glGetIntegerv(GL_VIEWPORT, vp);
	glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, fbo_);
	glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, tgt, 0);
	const GLenum db = GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0;
	glDrawBuffers(1, &db);
	if (!fbo_checked_ && glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER) != GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE) {
		glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0);
		if (!logged_fail_) {
			logged_fail_ = true;
			dlog("gpu: framebuffer incomplete; falling back to the CPU path");
		}
		return false;
	}
	fbo_checked_ = true;
	glViewport(0, 0, sw, sh);
	glUseProgram(program_);
	glUniform1i(u_y_tex_, 0);
	glUniform1i(u_c_tex_, 1);
	glUniform1i(u_v_tex_, 2);
	glUniform1i(u_pq_tex_, 3);
	glUniform1i(u_colors_, pic.colors == YuvColors::Hdr10 ? 2 : pic.colors == YuvColors::Hlg ? 3 : pic.colors == YuvColors::DoviP5 ? 4 : pic.colors == YuvColors::Bt601 ? 0 : 1);
	glUniform1i(u_interleaved_, pic.planes.interleaved ? 1 : 0);
	glUniform1f(u_peak_, pic.planes.wide ? 65535.0f : 1020.0f);
	glUniform1f(u_shift_div_, pic.planes.wide && pic.planes.shift ? 64.0f : 1.0f);
	glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tex_y_);
	glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE1);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tex_c_);
	glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE2);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tex_v_);
	glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE3);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tex_pq_);
	glBindVertexArray(vao_);
	glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 3);
	bool drawn = gl_ok("yuv draw");
	// Leave the GL state as the toolkit expects it.
	glBindVertexArray(0);
	for (int unit = 3; unit >= 0; --unit) {
		glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0 + unit);
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
	}
	glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0);
	glUseProgram(0);
	glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0);
	glViewport(vp[0], vp[1], vp[2], vp[3]);
	if (!drawn) return false;
	target = tgt;
	return true;
}


===== FILE: gl/gpu_convert.hpp =====
// The video picture's YUV->RGB conversion on the GPU: the decoded planes go
// up as textures and a fragment shader does the YUV->RGB matrix plus the
// HDR10 tone mapping (the same math as src/yuv_convert.cpp, in float).
//
// Fail-closed by design, and never required for correct playback:
//   - ensure() returns false when anything is unsupported (shaders, texture
//     formats); the caller then keeps the CPU path for the whole stream.
//   - render() returns false on any GL failure; the caller converts the same
//     planes on the CPU instead (yuv_convert.h).
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

#include "player.h"  // Player::Picture

class GpuYuv {
public:
	GpuYuv() = default;
	// No GL calls: the app exits through a noreturn quit(), so this never
	// runs with a dead context; while running, the objects are tiny and the
	// textures are recycled on size changes.
	~GpuYuv() = default;
	GpuYuv(const GpuYuv&) = delete;
	GpuYuv& operator=(const GpuYuv&) = delete;

	// Compile the shaders and build the PQ LUT. Must be called with the GL
	// context current (the UI thread). False when the GPU path can't be
	// used; logs once.
	bool ensure();
	bool ready() const { return program_ != 0; }

	// Upload the picture's planes and render YUV->RGB into target, an RGBA
	// texture the caller owns (recreated when the size changes; tw/th track
	// it). False on any GL failure: convert on the CPU instead.
	bool render(const Player::Picture& pic, std::uint32_t& target, int& tw, int& th);

private:
	bool upload_planes(const Player::Picture& pic);
	// Drain glGetError, logging the first failure site.
	bool gl_ok(const char* what);

	unsigned program_ = 0, vao_ = 0, fbo_ = 0;
	unsigned tex_y_ = 0, tex_c_ = 0, tex_v_ = 0, tex_pq_ = 0;
	int u_y_tex_ = -1, u_c_tex_ = -1, u_v_tex_ = -1, u_pq_tex_ = -1;
	int u_colors_ = -1, u_interleaved_ = -1, u_peak_ = -1, u_shift_div_ = -1;
	int py_w_ = 0, py_h_ = 0, pc_w_ = 0, pc_h_ = 0;  // plane texture sizes
	bool wide_ = false, interleaved_ = false;        // plane texture formats
	bool logged_fail_ = false;
	bool fbo_checked_ = false;  // framebuffer completeness only changes when the target texture is (re)allocated
};


===== FILE: gl/ime.cpp =====
#include "ime.hpp"

#include "util.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>

#ifdef PLATFORM_PS5_NATIVE

extern "C"
{
    int sceUserServiceInitialize(const void *params);
    int sceUserServiceGetForegroundUser(int *user);
    int sceImeDialogInit(const void *param, const void *extended);
    int sceImeDialogGetStatus(void);
    int sceImeDialogGetResult(void *result);
    int sceImeDialogTerm(void);
}

namespace sx
{

namespace
{

// OrbisImeDialogSetting. SDL's driver for the console fills in only the user, the
// length and the buffer, and leaves everything else zero; so does this, apart from where
// the dialog is put.
struct ImeParam
{
    std::uint32_t user_id;
    std::uint32_t type;
    std::uint64_t supported_languages;
    std::int32_t enter_label;
    std::int32_t input_method;
    void *filter;
    std::uint32_t option;
    std::uint32_t max_text_length;
    std::uint16_t *buffer;
    float pos_x, pos_y;
    std::int32_t horizontal_alignment, vertical_alignment;
    const std::uint16_t *placeholder;
    const std::uint16_t *title;
    std::uint8_t reserved[16];
};
static_assert(sizeof(ImeParam) == 96, "the dialog's setting is 96 bytes");

struct ImeResult
{
    std::int32_t end_status; // 0: the user accepted the text; 1 and 2: closed
    std::int32_t reserved[12];
};

constexpr int kMaxChars = 2048;
constexpr int kRunning = 1, kFinished = 2;
std::uint16_t g_text[kMaxChars + 8];
ImeParam g_param;

// The dialog writes UTF-16. Some firmware versions have been seen to widen the
// units to 32 bits; both are read.
std::string utf8_of(const std::uint16_t *u)
{
    const bool wide = u[0] != 0 && u[1] == 0 && u[2] != 0;
    std::string out;
    const auto put = [&](std::uint32_t cp) {
        if (cp < 0x80)
            out += static_cast<char>(cp);
        else if (cp < 0x800)
        {
            out += static_cast<char>(0xC0 | (cp >> 6));
            out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));
        }
        else if (cp < 0x10000)
        {
            out += static_cast<char>(0xE0 | (cp >> 12));
            out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F));
            out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));
        }
        else
        {
            out += static_cast<char>(0xF0 | (cp >> 18));
            out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F));
            out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F));
            out += static_cast<char>(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F));
        }
    };
    const int step = wide ? 2 : 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < kMaxChars; i += step)
    {
        std::uint32_t c = u[i];
        if (c == 0)
            break;
        if (c >= 0xD800 && c < 0xDC00 && u[i + step] >= 0xDC00 && u[i + step] < 0xE000)
        {
            c = 0x10000 + ((c - 0xD800) << 10) + (u[i + step] - 0xDC00);
            i += step;
        }
        put(c);
    }
    return out;
}

} // namespace

bool Ime::open()
{
    if (active_)
        return true;
    const int init = sceUserServiceInitialize(nullptr);
    (void)init; // already initialised is fine
    int user = 0;
    if (sceUserServiceGetForegroundUser(&user) != 0)
    {
        dlog("ime: no foreground user");
        return false;
    }
    std::memset(g_text, 0, sizeof(g_text));
    std::memset(&g_param, 0, sizeof(g_param));
    g_param.user_id = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(user);
    g_param.max_text_length = kMaxChars;
    g_param.buffer = g_text;
    // The dialog sits at the top right, not in the corner it opens in by default: its top right corner
    // is put at this point of the 1920 x 1080 screen (alignments: 0 left/top, 1 centre, 2 right/bottom).
    g_param.horizontal_alignment = 2;
    g_param.vertical_alignment = 0;
    g_param.pos_x = 1890.0f;
    g_param.pos_y = 30.0f;
    const int r = sceImeDialogInit(&g_param, nullptr);
    if (r != 0)
    {
        dlog("ime: sceImeDialogInit 0x%08x", static_cast<unsigned>(r));
        return false;
    }
    active_ = true;
    seen_running_ = false;
    opened_ = now_seconds();
    return true;
}

Ime::State Ime::poll(std::string *text)
{
    if (!active_)
        return State::idle;
    const int status = sceImeDialogGetStatus();
    if (status == kRunning)
    {
        seen_running_ = true;
        return State::open;
    }
    if (status != kFinished)
    {
        // Never started: give up after a few seconds rather than wait for ever.
        if (!seen_running_ && now_seconds() - opened_ > 3.0)
        {
            sceImeDialogTerm();
            active_ = false;
            return State::cancelled;
        }
        return seen_running_ ? State::cancelled : State::open;
    }
    ImeResult result;
    std::memset(&result, 0, sizeof(result));
    State out = State::cancelled;
    if (sceImeDialogGetResult(&result) == 0 && result.end_status == 0)
    {
        if (text)
            *text = utf8_of(g_text);
        out = State::done;
    }
    sceImeDialogTerm();
    active_ = false;
    return out;
}

} // namespace sx

#else // not on the console: there is no keyboard dialog

namespace sx
{
bool Ime::open()
{
    return false;
}
Ime::State Ime::poll(std::string *)
{
    return State::idle;
}
} // namespace sx

#endif


===== FILE: gl/ime.hpp =====
// The console's own keyboard (libSceImeDialog): a full-screen dialog that takes
// the controller while it is up and hands back what was typed. The app only
// asks for it and waits.

#pragma once

#include <string>

namespace sx
{

class Ime
{
  public:
    enum class State
    {
        idle,      // no dialog
        open,      // the dialog is up
        done,      // the user finished: text is set
        cancelled, // the user closed it
    };

    // Opens the dialog; false if the console would not (or this is not a console).
    bool open();
    // Once per frame while a dialog is up.
    State poll(std::string *text);
    bool active() const
    {
        return active_;
    }

  private:
    bool active_ = false;
    double opened_ = 0.0;
    bool seen_running_ = false;
};

} // namespace sx


===== FILE: gl/main.cpp =====
// Stremio for the PS5 on the OpenGL toolkit: opens the display and the
// controller, then runs the frame loop. What the buttons mean is ui/shell.cpp,
// what the screens show is gl/session.cpp.

#include "chrome.hpp"
#include "core/input.hpp"
#include "dynamic_font.hpp"
#include "gfx/renderer.hpp"
#include "hdr_probe.h"
#include "hwdec_ps5.h"
#include "platform/ps5/display_egl.hpp"
#include "platform/ps5/pad.hpp"
#include "platform/ps5/system.hpp"
#include "overlays.hpp"
#include "page.hpp"
#include "session.hpp"
#include "shell.hpp"
#include "theme.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <csignal>
#include <cstdio>
#include <span>
#include <string>

extern "C" void ps5_load_modules(void); // the keyboard dialog's module (native/ps5_modules.c)

#define STB_IMAGE_STATIC
#define STB_IMAGE_IMPLEMENTATION
#define STBI_NO_HDR
#define STBI_NO_LINEAR
#include "stb_image.h"

namespace
{

constexpr const char *kRoot = "/app0";
// The title's own storage (param.json downloadDataSize): settings, progress, artwork.
constexpr const char *kData = "/download0/stremio";

struct Mode
{
    int width, height;
};

// 4K first, then what a 1080p television can show.
constexpr Mode kModes[] = {{3840, 2160}, {1920, 1080}};

std::uint32_t load_icon(hui::gfx::Renderer &renderer, const std::string &path)
{
    int w = 0, h = 0, comp = 0;
    unsigned char *pixels = stbi_load(path.c_str(), &w, &h, &comp, 4);
    if (!pixels)
    {
        hui::sys::log("[SX] cannot load %s", path.c_str());
        return 0;
    }
    const std::uint32_t texture = renderer.batch().create_texture(w, h, pixels);
    stbi_image_free(pixels);
    return texture;
}

} // namespace

int main()
{
    using namespace hui;
    sys::log("[SX] entry");
    const std::string root = kRoot;
    // A closed connection must fail a write quietly instead of killing us.
    std::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);

    ps5::Display display;
    bool opened = false;
    for (const Mode &mode : kModes)
    {
        if (display.open(mode.width, mode.height))
        {
            opened = true;
            sys::log("[SX] display %dx%d", display.width(), display.height());
            break;
        }
        sys::log("[SX] display %dx%d failed", mode.width, mode.height);
    }
    if (!opened)
        sys::park();

    // One-time HDR10 signal probe: runs while the screen is still black,
    // before the first frame. Probe-only, rolls back to SDR immediately.
    hdr_probe::hdr_signal_probe(display.width(), display.height());

    gfx::Renderer renderer;
    static sx::UiFonts ui_fonts;
    static ui::Fonts fonts;
    if (!renderer.init())
    {
        sys::log("[SX] fatal: renderer failed");
        sys::park();
    }

    // The boot animation starts as early as it can: its first frame is the picture the console shows
    // while the app starts (sce_sys/pic0 and pic1: the page's light and the mark), so nothing cuts when we
    // take over, and everything slow (the modules, fonts, storage, the network) happens after it, with a frame of the
    // animation drawn between the steps.
    static sx::Icons icons;
    const std::string icon_dir = root + "/icons";
    icons.logo_xl = load_icon(renderer, icon_dir + "/logo_xl.png");
    icons.name = load_icon(renderer, icon_dir + "/name.png");
    const std::int64_t boot_t0 = sys::monotonic_us();
    const auto boot_seconds = [&] { return static_cast<float>(sys::monotonic_us() - boot_t0) / 1e6f; };
    bool splash_hidden = false;
    const auto boot_frame = [&] {
        const sx::Env boot_env{fonts, icons};
        gfx::DrawList list;
        gfx::BackdropSpec backdrop;
        sx::apply_page_backdrop(backdrop, boot_seconds());
        sx::draw_boot(list, boot_env, boot_seconds(), 0.0f);
        renderer.begin();
        renderer.backdrop(backdrop);
        renderer.draw(list);
        renderer.present(0, display.width(), display.height());
        if (!display.swap())
        {
            sys::log("[SX] fatal: boot swap failed");
            sys::park();
        }
        if (!splash_hidden)
        {
            splash_hidden = true;
            sys::log("[SX] first picture; splash hidden: %d", sys::hide_splash_screen() ? 1 : 0);
        }
    };
    boot_frame();
    ps5_load_modules(); // the keyboard dialog
    boot_frame();
    HwDecoder::load_module(); // the hardware video decoder
    boot_frame();
    if (!sx::load_ui_fonts(renderer, root + "/fonts", root + "/hui-fonts", &ui_fonts, &fonts))
    {
        sys::log("[SX] fatal: fonts failed");
        sys::park();
    }
    boot_frame();

    const char *solid[5] = {"nav_board", "nav_discover", "nav_library", "nav_addons", "nav_settings"};
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; ++i)
    {
        icons.nav_solid[i] = load_icon(renderer, icon_dir + "/" + solid[i] + ".png");
        icons.nav_line[i] = load_icon(renderer, icon_dir + "/" + solid[i] + "_o.png");
    }
    icons.search = load_icon(renderer, icon_dir + "/search.png");
    icons.logo = load_icon(renderer, icon_dir + "/logo_l.png");
    boot_frame();

    static sx::Session session;
    if (!session.init(root, kData, &renderer))
    {
        sys::log("[SX] fatal: session failed");
        sys::park();
    }
    // One-time warning if Thai fonts are missing: Thai subtitles will render
    // as '?' without them. The dlog in load_ui_fonts has the details.
    if (!ui_fonts.missing_thai_fonts.empty())
    {
        std::string names;
        for (const std::string &f : ui_fonts.missing_thai_fonts)
        {
            if (!names.empty())
                names += ", ";
            names += f;
        }
        session.say("Missing Thai fonts (" + names + ") - Thai subtitles may show as '?'.", 8.0, true);
    }
    // The display's real size: the player may emit 4K video frames when the
    // GPU conversion path is active and the display is a 2160p mode.
    session.set_display_size(display.width(), display.height());
    static sx::Env env{fonts, icons};
    static sx::Shell shell(env, session);
    shell.start_sound(root + "/sounds"); // the interface's sounds
    shell.start_boot_at(boot_seconds()); // the animation goes on from where the frames above left it

    ps5::Pad pad;
    pad.open();
    InputTracker tracker;
    PadSample samples[64];

    std::uint64_t frames = 0;
    std::int64_t last_start = sys::monotonic_us();
    std::int64_t window_start = last_start;
    int window_frames = 0;
    float worst_ms = 0.0f;
    for (;;)
    {
        const std::int64_t now = sys::monotonic_us();
        float dt = frames == 0 ? 1.0f / 60.0f : static_cast<float>(now - last_start) / 1e6f;
        last_start = now;
        const float frame_ms = dt * 1000.0f;
        dt = std::min(dt, 0.05f); // a hitch must not teleport the animations

        const std::size_t count = pad.read(samples);
        const InputFrame input = tracker.update(std::span<const PadSample>(samples, count), static_cast<std::uint64_t>(now));
        session.update(dt, shell.cursor());
        env.clock = session.clock;
        shell.update(input, dt);
        if (session.wants_exit())
        {
            // Shut down first: flush progress, stop the torrent engine and
            // its threads, and remove the UPnP router mapping. quitting
            // without this leaves the mappings behind on the router.
            session.shutdown();
            sys::quit();
        }

        // Glass Phase 1: the frame is two layers. bg holds the page content
        // (artwork, text, cards); glass() blurs it into the renderer's glass
        // texture; fg holds the frosted-glass panels, which sample that blur.
        gfx::DrawList bg, fg;
        gfx::BackdropSpec backdrop;
        shell.draw(bg, fg, backdrop);
        sx::sync_fonts(renderer, ui_fonts, fonts);
        renderer.begin();
        renderer.backdrop(backdrop);
        renderer.draw(bg);
        // The blur pass is pure waste when nothing glassy will draw (e.g.
        // video playback with the OSD hidden): skip it and keep the last
        // texture, which nobody samples while fg is empty.
        if (!fg.empty())
        {
            renderer.glass();
            env.glass_tex = renderer.glass_texture();
        }
        renderer.draw(fg);
        renderer.present(0, display.width(), display.height());
        if (!display.swap())
        {
            sys::log("[SX] fatal: swap failed at frame %llu", static_cast<unsigned long long>(frames));
            sys::park();
        }
        ++frames;
        if (frames == 1)
        {
            sys::log("[SX] first frame: %zu shapes, %zu draw calls", renderer.last_instances(), renderer.last_draw_calls());
        }

        // One line every ten seconds: how fast the frames came.
        ++window_frames;
        worst_ms = std::max(worst_ms, frame_ms);
        if (now - window_start >= 10'000'000)
        {
            const double seconds = static_cast<double>(now - window_start) / 1e6;
            sys::log("[SX] %.1f fps, worst frame %.1f ms, %zu shapes, %zu draw calls", window_frames / seconds, worst_ms,
                     renderer.last_instances(), renderer.last_draw_calls());
            window_start = now;
            window_frames = 0;
            worst_ms = 0.0f;
        }
    }
}

// What the app knows about, apart from how it is drawn: something that can be

#pragma once

// Something that can be opened: a catalog entry, a library item.
struct Item
{
    std::string id, type, name, poster, background, logo;
    std::string description, release_info, runtime, imdb_rating;
    std::vector<std::string> genres;
    // Continue watching
    std::string video_id;
    double offset = 0, duration = 0; // seconds
    std::int64_t last_watched = 0;   // epoch ms
    int times_watched = 0;
    bool up_next = false; // video_id is the episode after one that was finished (nothing watched of it yet)
};

Item item_from_meta_json(const json &j);

// Where a title was left, for people who are not signed in.
struct Progress
{
    std::string type, name, poster, video_id;
    double time = 0, duration = 0;
    std::int64_t updated = 0;
    // The stream (as JSON) that was playing and the episode it was for: Continue Watching plays it again.
    std::string stream_json, stream_video_id;
    // The episode after the one that was just finished, until something of it is watched.
    std::string up_next;
};

struct Prefs
{
    // Remembered audio/subtitle picks, per series or movie id: choosing a
    // track once applies it to every later episode of the same show.
    struct TrackMemory
    {
        std::string audio_lang; // "" = no remembered audio pick
        std::string sub_lang;   // "" = no remembered subtitle pick
        bool sub_internal = false; // the remembered sub was in-file (not addon)
        bool sub_off = false;      // remembered "subtitles off"
        double sub_delay = 0;      // remembered subtitle delay in seconds
    };
    std::string server_url;
    bool builtin_torrents = true; // the app's own torrent engine, no server needed
    std::string subtitle_langs = "eng";
    bool auto_subtitles = true;
    std::string sub_size = "sub-m";
    std::string audio_langs;
    int audio_output = 0;   // 0 = stereo downmix, 1 = discrete 5.1/7.1 PCM over HDMI
    int volume_boost = 100; // percent: 100, 125, 150, 200
    int volume = 100;       // master volume 0-100 (touchpad swipe); persisted
    bool night_mode = false;       // DRC: tame loud peaks, lift quiet dialogue
    bool dolby_passthrough = false; // bitstream AC-3 to the receiver (opt-in)
    bool match_frame_rate = false;  // experimental: switch HDMI to 119.88 Hz for ~24fps film
    bool autoplay_next = true;
    bool autoplay_best = true; // play the best stream without showing the picker
    int binge_ask = 3;         // "Still watching?" after this many automatic episodes; 0 = off
    std::string sub_color = "white"; // subtitle text color: "white" | "yellow"
    int sub_bg_opacity = 55;        // subtitle background darkness, 0-100 (0 = no box)
    std::string sub_pos = "bottom";  // subtitle position: "bottom" | "raised"
    std::string aspect_mode = "fit";   // video zoom: "fit" (whole picture) | "fill" (crop to screen)
    bool ui_sounds = true; // the interface's soft sounds
    int skip_mode = 0;     // intro/outro skip: 0 off, 1 prompt, 2 auto
    int disc_sort = 0;     // discover sort: 0 default (catalog order), 1 rating, 2 year (newest)
    std::string max_resolution = "auto"; // stream cap: "auto" | "4k" | "1080p" | "720p" | "480p"
    std::string os_user; // OpenSubtitles.com username (for a supporting subtitle addon)
    std::string os_pass; // OpenSubtitles.com password (stored locally, never synced)
    double audio_delay = 0.0; // audio lip-sync offset in seconds, -0.5..+0.5 (+ = audio later)
    int upscaler = 1; // video upscaler: 0 off, 1 FSR1, 2 FSR1+sharpening (3 Anime4K reserved)
    double upscaler_sharpness = 0.5; // RCAS strength 0.0-1.0, for upscaler == 2
    std::map<std::string, int> aniskip_mal; // series id -> MyAnimeList id, for intro/outro lookup
    // TheIntroDB skip-segment cache: "tidb:<imdbid>" (movie) or
    // "tidb:<imdbid>:<season>:<episode>" -> fetch time + segments. An empty
    // segment list is a negative entry: the title definitively has no data.
    struct SkipDbEntry
    {
        double fetched_at = 0; // unix epoch seconds
        std::vector<aniskip::SkipSegment> segs;
    };
    std::map<std::string, SkipDbEntry> skipdb_cache;
    std::vector<std::string> extra_addons;
    std::set<std::string> disabled_addons; // transport_urls the user turned off on the Addons page
    std::vector<std::string> addon_order;  // transport_urls in the user's priority order
    std::string auth_key, user_email;
    std::map<std::string, TrackMemory> track_memory; // series/movie id -> picks
};

// One catalog of one addon, shown as a row on the Board.

    Catalog catalog;

std::string size_label(const std::string &s)
{
    if (s == "sub-s")
        return "Small";
    if (s == "sub-l")
        return "Large";
    return "Medium";
}

std::string subcolor_label(const std::string &s)
{
    return s == "yellow" ? "Yellow" : "White";
}

std::string format_bytes(std::uint64_t n)
{
    char buf[32];
    if (n >= 1ull << 30)
        std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%.1f GB", n / double(1ull << 30));
    else if (n >= 1ull << 20)
        std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%.1f MB", n / double(1ull << 20));
    else if (n >= 1ull << 10)
        std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%llu KB", static_cast<unsigned long long>((n + 512) >> 10));
    else
        std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%llu B", static_cast<unsigned long long>(n));
    return buf;
}

std::string subpos_label(const std::string &s)
{
    return s == "raised" ? "Raised" : "Bottom";
}

std::string binge_label(int v)
{
    return v <= 0 ? "Off" : "After " + std::to_string(v) + " episodes";
}

{
    return v == 1 ? "Surround (5.1/7.1 PCM)" : "Stereo";
}

}

}

        return "4K";
    if (s == "1080p")

    if (s == "720p")

}

std::string upscale_label(int m)

    switch (m) {
    case 1: return "FSR1";
    case 2: return "FSR1 + Sharpening";
    default: return "Off";
    }
}

// The first letter of a name (one UTF-8 character): an addon's mark when it has no logo.
std::string first_letter(const std::string &name)
{
    std::size_t len = name.empty() ? 0 : 1;
    while (len < name.size() && (static_cast<unsigned char>(name[len]) & 0xC0) == 0x80)
        ++len;
    return name.substr(0, len);
}

std::uint32_t colour_for(const std::string &name)
{
    static const std::uint32_t palette[] = {0x7b5bf5, 0x3b82f6, 0x0ea5a4, 0xe0568a, 0xe08a3c, 0x6d6ae0};
    return palette[fnv1a(name) % (sizeof(palette) / sizeof(palette[0]))];
}
