            playing.skip_prompt = "Skip " + aniskip::kind_label(sg.kind);
        }
    }
}

void Session::watch_auto_subtitles()
{
    if (!prefs_.auto_subtitles || w_auto_sub_done_ || w_sub_active_ >= 0)
        return;
    // A remembered pick for this show outranks the generic auto-select.
    const Prefs::TrackMemory *mem = nullptr;
    {
        const std::string key = watch_memory_key();
        if (!key.empty())
        {
            const auto it = prefs_.track_memory.find(key);
            if (it != prefs_.track_memory.end())
                mem = &it->second;
        }
    }
    if (mem && mem->sub_off)
    {
        w_auto_sub_done_ = true; // remembered "off": stay silent
        return;
    }
    if (mem && !mem->sub_lang.empty())
    {
        int best = -1, best_rank = 100;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w_subs_.size(); ++i)
        {
            const WatchSub &s = w_subs_[i];
            if (s.lang != mem->sub_lang || (s.embedded >= 0) != mem->sub_internal)
                continue;
            const int r = sub_auto_rank(s, mem->sub_lang);
            if (r < best_rank)
            {
                best_rank = r;
                best = static_cast<int>(i);
            }
        }
        if (best >= 0)
        {
            w_auto_sub_done_ = true;
            w_sub_auto_ = true;
            watch_select_sub(best);
            return;
        }
        // No match yet — the right tracks may still be arriving; fall through
        // to the generic pick. If it locks in, the late-arriving embedded
        // tracks still trigger a re-pick above, which retries this memory.
    }
    for (const auto &lang : pref_langs(prefs_.subtitle_langs))
    {
        // Do not pick subtitles in the language being heard.
        bool heard = false;
        for (const auto &t : player_.audio_tracks())
            if (t.stream == player_.audio_stream() && t.lang == lang)
                heard = true;
        if (heard)
        {
            w_auto_sub_done_ = true;
            return;
        }
        // Pick the best track: internal (embedded) subtitles before external
        // ones, and skip junk tracks (signs/songs-only) unless nothing better
        // exists. Cue counts are only parsed once a track is used, so at
        // auto-select time the label heuristic does most of the work (EVO's
        // MIN_USEFUL_CUES rule); the cue gate applies where counts are known.
        int best = -1, best_rank = 100;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w_subs_.size(); ++i)
        {
            const int r = sub_auto_rank(w_subs_[i], lang);
            if (r < best_rank)
            {
                best_rank = r;
                best = static_cast<int>(i);
            }
        }
        if (best >= 0)
        {
            w_auto_sub_done_ = true;
            w_sub_auto_ = true;
            watch_select_sub(best);
            return;
        }
    }
    // Last resort: when nothing carried a language tag, a single untagged
    // embedded track is probably the right one.
    w_auto_sub_done_ = true;
    int untagged = -1, untagged_count = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w_subs_.size(); ++i)
        if (w_subs_[i].embedded >= 0 && w_subs_[i].lang.empty())
        {
            ++untagged_count;
            untagged = static_cast<int>(i);
        }
    if (untagged_count == 1)
    {
        w_sub_auto_ = true;
        watch_select_sub(untagged);
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The next episode

const ::Video *Session::next_episode() const
{
    const auto &vids = d_meta_.videos;
    std::size_t cur = vids.size();
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < vids.size(); ++i)
        if (vids[i].id == w_video_id_)
            cur = i;
    if (cur + 1 >= vids.size())
        return nullptr;
    const ::Video &next = vids[cur + 1];
    if (next.season == 0 && vids[cur].season != 0)
        return nullptr; // do not roll into the specials
    return &next;
}

std::string Session::episode_heading(const ::Video &v)
{
    std::string heading = "S" + std::to_string(v.season) + " E" + std::to_string(v.episode);
    if (!v.title.empty())
        heading += "  \xC2\xB7  " + v.title;
    return heading;
}

void Session::watch_upnext_fire(bool manual)
{
    if (manual)
        w_binge_count_ = 0;
    else if (watch_binge_check())
        return; // "Still watching?" is up instead of advancing
    // The union of what the two countdown-zero paths did: clear the card,
    // mark the episode finished (idempotent — the Ended path already saved),
    // and roll into the next episode.
    w_upnext_until_ = 0;
    w_upnext_heading_.clear();
    playing.upnext_title.clear();
    playing.upnext_remaining = -1;
    watch_save_progress(true, true);
    watch_stop(true);
    watch_next_episode();
}

// An automatic advance is about to happen: the binge guard counts it and,
// once the threshold is reached, puts up the "Still watching?" prompt
// instead. Returns true when it intercepted (no advance happened).
bool Session::watch_binge_check()
{
    const int threshold = prefs_.binge_ask;
    if (threshold <= 0 || !prefs_.autoplay_next)
        return false;
    ++w_binge_count_;
    if (w_binge_count_ < threshold)
        return false;
    w_binge_asking_ = true;
    w_binge_left_ = kBingeTimeoutSecs;
    w_binge_prev_ = 0;
    w_upnext_heading_.clear();
    w_upnext_until_ = 0;
    playing.upnext_title.clear();
    playing.upnext_remaining = -1;
    playing.binge_prompt = true;
    playing.binge_left = w_binge_left_;
    return true;
}

void Session::watch_next_episode()
{
    const ::Video *next = next_episode();
    if (!next)
        return;

    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < d_seasons_.size(); ++i)
        if (d_seasons_[i] == next->season && static_cast<int>(i) != d_season_idx_)
            detail_set_season(static_cast<int>(i));
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < d_season_videos_.size(); ++i)
        if (d_season_videos_[i]->id == next->id)
        {
            detail.episode_hint = static_cast<int>(i);
            ++detail.hint_serial;
        }

    autoplay_pending_ = true;
    autobest_pending_ = false; // the binge pick owns stream selection from here
    autoplay_binge_ = w_stream_.binge_group;
    autoplay_addon_ = w_stream_.addon;
    w_binge_auto_ = true; // the play_stream this triggers must not reset the binge count
    std::string heading = episode_heading(*next);
    detail_load_streams(next->id, heading);
    say("Next: " + heading);
}

} // namespace sx


===== FILE: gl/stream_json.hpp =====
// A stream (what was playing) as JSON, so that Continue Watching can play it again.

#pragma once

#include "stremio.h"
#include "util.h"

#include <string>
#include <vector>

inline json stream_to_json(const ::Stream &s)
{
    json j;
    j["name"] = s.name;
    j["description"] = s.description;
    j["addon"] = s.addon;
    j["url"] = s.url;
    j["info_hash"] = s.info_hash;
    j["file_idx"] = s.file_idx;
    j["sources"] = s.sources;
    j["filename"] = s.filename;
    j["binge_group"] = s.binge_group;
    j["not_web_ready"] = s.not_web_ready;
    j["request_headers"] = s.request_headers;
    return j;
}

inline ::Stream stream_from_json(const json &j)
{
    ::Stream s;
    s.name = jstr(j, "name");
    s.description = jstr(j, "description");
    s.addon = jstr(j, "addon");
    s.url = jstr(j, "url");
    s.info_hash = jstr(j, "info_hash");
    s.file_idx = j.contains("file_idx") && j["file_idx"].is_number_integer() ? j["file_idx"].get<int>() : -1;
    const auto strings = [&](const char *key, std::vector<std::string> &out) {
        if (j.contains(key) && j[key].is_array())
            for (const auto &v : j[key])
                if (v.is_string())
                    out.push_back(v.get<std::string>());
    };
    strings("sources", s.sources);
    strings("request_headers", s.request_headers);
    s.filename = jstr(j, "filename");
    s.binge_group = jstr(j, "binge_group");
    s.not_web_ready = jbool(j, "not_web_ready", false);
    return s;
}

===== FILE: gl/system_status.cpp =====
#include "system_status.hpp"

#include "util.h"

#include <cstring>

#ifdef PLATFORM_PS5
extern "C" int sceSystemServiceGetStatus(void *status);
#endif

namespace sx
{

SystemStatus read_system_status()
{
    SystemStatus out;
#ifdef PLATFORM_PS5
    // The console's status record: the event count, then flags (SceSystemServiceStatus: byte 4 is
    // isSystemUiOverlaid, byte 5 isInBackgroundExecution). What it holds is logged when it changes, so
    // that a console that reports it differently can be seen in the log.
    alignas(8) unsigned char raw[256];
    std::memset(raw, 0, sizeof(raw));
    static bool failed = false;
    if (failed)
        return out;
    const int r = sceSystemServiceGetStatus(raw);
    if (r != 0)
    {
        failed = true;
        dlog("system status: sceSystemServiceGetStatus 0x%08x (not used)", static_cast<unsigned>(r));
        return out;
    }
    static unsigned char last[16];
    static bool first = true;
    if (first || std::memcmp(last, raw, sizeof(last)) != 0)
    {
        first = false;
        std::memcpy(last, raw, sizeof(last));
        dlog("system status: %02x%02x%02x%02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x", raw[0], raw[1], raw[2], raw[3], raw[4],
             raw[5], raw[6], raw[7], raw[8], raw[9], raw[10], raw[11]);
    }
    out.valid = true;
    out.overlaid = raw[4] != 0;
    out.background = raw[5] != 0;
#endif
    return out;
}

} // namespace sx

===== FILE: gl/touchpad.cpp =====
#include "touchpad.hpp"

#include <cstring>

namespace sx
{
namespace
{

// scePad NIDs (resolved at runtime like the other pad calls).
extern "C"
{
    int sceUserServiceGetInitialUser(int *user);
    int scePadInit(void);
    int scePadOpen(int user, int type, int index, const void *parameters);
    int scePadClose(int handle);
    int scePadRead(int handle, void *samples, int count);
}

// 120-byte ScePadData: we only care about the touch region.
struct RawTouchSample
{
    std::uint8_t pad[0x34];      // buttons, sticks, triggers, motion
    std::uint8_t touch_count;    // 0x34
    std::uint8_t reserved[7];    // 0x35-0x3B
    std::uint8_t touch0[8];      // 0x3C-0x43
    std::uint8_t touch1[8];      // 0x44-0x4B
    std::uint8_t rest[0x78 - 0x4C]; // connected, timestamp, etc.
};
static_assert(sizeof(RawTouchSample) == 120);

bool parse_touch_point(const std::uint8_t *bytes, TouchPoint &out)
{
    // Bit 7 of the ID byte = finger lifted.
    if (bytes[0] & 0x80)
    {
        out.active = false;
        return false;
    }
    out.active = true;
    // 12-bit little-endian coordinates.
    out.x = (bytes[1] | ((bytes[2] & 0x0F) << 8)) & 0xFFF;
    out.y = (bytes[3] | ((bytes[4] & 0x0F) << 8)) & 0xFFF;
    // Clamp to the DualSense pad's 1920x1080 range.
    if (out.x > 1919)
        out.x = 1919;
    if (out.y > 1079)
        out.y = 1079;
    return true;
}

} // namespace

TouchpadReader::~TouchpadReader()
{
    close();
}

bool TouchpadReader::open()
{
    if (handle_ >= 0)
        return true;
    int user = -1;
    if (sceUserServiceGetInitialUser(&user) != 0 || user < 0)
        return false;
    scePadInit();
    // A second read-only open to the same controller. If the system
    // rejects it (handle < 0), swipe volume stays disabled.
    handle_ = scePadOpen(user, 0, 0, nullptr);
    return handle_ >= 0;
}

void TouchpadReader::close()
{
    if (handle_ >= 0)
    {
        scePadClose(handle_);
        handle_ = -1;
    }
}

bool TouchpadReader::poll(TouchPoint &point)
{
    point.active = false;
    if (handle_ < 0)
        return false;
    // Read up to 8 samples; use the newest for current touch state.
    RawTouchSample samples[8];
    const int count = scePadRead(handle_, samples, 8);
    if (count <= 0)
        return false;
    const RawTouchSample &s = samples[count - 1];
    if (s.touch_count == 0)
        return false;
    // Use the first active finger.
    if (parse_touch_point(s.touch0, point))
        return true;
    return parse_touch_point(s.touch1, point);
}

} // namespace sx


===== FILE: gl/touchpad.hpp =====
#pragma once
// DualSense touchpad swipe reader for volume control.
//
// Parses the touch data from scePadRead's 120-byte ScePadData records.
// Layout (from PS5 homebrew research):
//   0x34: touch count (1 byte)
//   0x3C: touch point 0 (8 bytes)
//   0x44: touch point 1 (8 bytes)
//
// Each 8-byte touch point:
//   byte 0: contact ID, bit 7 set = finger lifted/inactive
//   bytes 1-2: X coordinate (12-bit LE, 0-1919)
//   bytes 3-4: Y coordinate (12-bit LE, 0-1079)
//   bytes 5-7: reserved
//
// This opens its own scePad handle (read-only). If the open fails
// (e.g. hui already holds the controller exclusively), the reader
// stays inert and swipe volume is silently unavailable.

#include <cstdint>

namespace sx
{

struct TouchPoint
{
    bool active = false; // finger currently touching
    int x = 0;           // 0-1919
    int y = 0;           // 0-1079, 0 = top of pad
};

class TouchpadReader
{
  public:
    TouchpadReader() = default;
    TouchpadReader(const TouchpadReader &) = delete;
    TouchpadReader &operator=(const TouchpadReader &) = delete;
    ~TouchpadReader();

    // Open the controller. Returns true on success.
    bool open();
    void close();
    bool is_open() const { return handle_ >= 0; }

    // Poll for touch state. Call once per frame. Returns true if a
    // finger is currently touching (point filled in).
    bool poll(TouchPoint &point);

  private:
    int handle_ = -1;
};

} // namespace sx


===== FILE: gl/ui_sound.cpp =====
#include "ui_sound.hpp"

#include "pcm_out.h"
#include "util.h"

#ifdef PLATFORM_PS5
#include "audio/mixer.hpp"
#include "audio/wav.hpp"
#include "core/save_file.hpp"
#include "platform/ps5/audio_out.hpp"

#include <chrono>
#endif

namespace sx
{

#ifdef PLATFORM_PS5

namespace
{

using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;

// How soon the same cue may play again: moving along posters must not turn into a rattle.
double min_gap_seconds(hui::audio::Cue cue)
{
    using hui::audio::Cue;
    switch (cue)
    {
    case Cue::focus:
        return 0.045;
    case Cue::error:
        return 0.30;
    default:
        return 0.12;
    }
}

} // namespace

struct UiSound::Impl
{
    hui::audio::Mixer mixer;
    hui::audio::SoundBank bank;
    hui::ps5::AudioOut out;
    bool loaded = false;
    bool open = false;
    double back_in = 0.0; // seconds until the port is taken back from the player
    bool has_pending = false;
    hui::audio::Cue pending = hui::audio::Cue::focus;
    Clock::time_point last[static_cast<std::size_t>(hui::audio::Cue::count)]{};
};

UiSound::UiSound() : impl_(new Impl)
{
}

UiSound::~UiSound()
{
    if (impl_ && impl_->open)
    {
        impl_->out.stop();
        AudioPort::ui_holds = false;
    }
}

bool UiSound::start(const std::string &dir)
{
    // The sounds are loaded by name, one by one: the console does not list a folder reliably (the toolkit's
    // own loader needs an index.txt for that), and these ten are all there are.
    struct Entry
    {
        hui::audio::Cue cue;
        const char *file;
    };
    using hui::audio::Cue;
    static const Entry kSounds[] = {{Cue::focus, "focus_02.wav"},   {Cue::tab, "tab_01.wav"},       {Cue::back, "back_01.wav"},
                                    {Cue::toggle, "toggle_02.wav"}, {Cue::error, "error_01.wav"},   {Cue::notify, "notify_01.wav"},
                                    {Cue::launch, "launch_01.wav"}, {Cue::saved, "saved_01.wav"},   {Cue::resume, "resume_01.wav"},
                                    {Cue::welcome, "welcome_01.wav"}};
    int files = 0;
    for (const Entry &e : kSounds)
    {
        const std::string path = dir + "/glass/" + e.file;
        std::string data;
        if (!hui::save::read_file(path, &data, 4u << 20))
        {
            dlog("sound: cannot read %s", path.c_str());
            continue;
        }
        hui::audio::DecodedWav wav = hui::audio::decode_wav(data);
        if (!wav.ok())
        {
            dlog("sound: %s: %s", e.file, wav.error.c_str());
            continue;
        }
        impl_->bank.add(hui::audio::SoundSet::glass, e.cue, std::move(wav.samples), wav.frames);
        ++files;
    }
    dlog("sound: %d of %zu sounds loaded from %s", files, sizeof(kSounds) / sizeof(kSounds[0]), dir.c_str());
    if (files == 0)
        return false;
    impl_->loaded = true;
    impl_->mixer.set_bus_gain(hui::audio::Bus::ui, 0.7f);
    impl_->mixer.set_bus_gain(hui::audio::Bus::sfx, 0.7f);
    if (!impl_->out.start(impl_->mixer))
    {
        dlog("sound: the audio port did not open");
        return false;
    }
    impl_->open = true;
    AudioPort::ui_holds = true;
    return true;
}

void UiSound::play(hui::audio::Cue cue)
{
    if (!enabled_ || !impl_->open)
        return;
    const std::size_t i = static_cast<std::size_t>(cue);
    const Clock::time_point now = Clock::now();
    if (std::chrono::duration<double>(now - impl_->last[i]).count() < min_gap_seconds(cue))
        return;
    impl_->last[i] = now;
    hui::audio::CueEvent event;
    event.cue = cue;
    event.set = hui::audio::SoundSet::glass;
    impl_->bank.play(impl_->mixer, hui::audio::SoundSet::glass, event);
}

void UiSound::play_when_back(hui::audio::Cue cue)
{
    if (impl_->open)
    {
        play(cue);
        return;
    }
    impl_->has_pending = true;
    impl_->pending = cue;
}

void UiSound::update(float dt)
{
    if (!impl_->loaded)
        return;
    if (AudioPort::player_wants.load())
    {
        // The player starts or is playing: it has the port.
        if (impl_->open)
        {
            impl_->out.stop();
            impl_->open = false;
            AudioPort::ui_holds = false;
        }
        impl_->back_in = 0.4;
        return;
    }
    if (!impl_->open)
    {
        impl_->back_in -= dt;
        if (impl_->back_in > 0.0)
            return;
        if (impl_->out.start(impl_->mixer))
        {
            impl_->open = true;
            AudioPort::ui_holds = true;
            if (impl_->has_pending)
            {
                impl_->has_pending = false;
                play(impl_->pending);
            }
        }
        else
        {
            impl_->back_in = 1.0; // try again in a moment
        }
    }
}

#else // on a PC the screens are only drawn: no sound

struct UiSound::Impl
{
};

UiSound::UiSound() : impl_(new Impl)
{
}

UiSound::~UiSound() = default;

bool UiSound::start(const std::string &)
{
    return false;
}

void UiSound::play(hui::audio::Cue)
{
}

void UiSound::play_when_back(hui::audio::Cue)
{
}

void UiSound::update(float)
{
}

#endif

===== FILE: gl/ui_sound.hpp =====
// The interface's sounds: soft sounds for moving around, going back, switching page and so on.
// They come from ps5-homebrew-ui's sound bank (the "glass" set, in <app>/sounds/glass) and play
// through its mixer on the console's audio port.
//
// The console gives the app one audio port at a time: while a video plays, the player has it.
// The player asks for it when it starts (AudioPort::player_wants) and this lets go of it, then
// takes it back when the player is done.

#pragma once

#include "audio/cues.hpp"

#include <memory>
#include <string>

namespace sx
{

class UiSound
{
  public:
    UiSound();
    ~UiSound();

    // Loads the sounds in <dir>/glass and opens the audio port. False: no sound (not fatal).
    bool start(const std::string &dir);
    // Plays a cue now. Cues asked for while the player has the port are dropped.
    void play(hui::audio::Cue cue);
    // Plays a cue as soon as the port is back (the player has just finished).
    void play_when_back(hui::audio::Cue cue);
    void set_enabled(bool on)
    {
        enabled_ = on;
    }
    // Once a frame: hands the port to the player and takes it back.
    void update(float dt);

  private:
    struct Impl;
    std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl_;
    bool enabled_ = true;
};

} // namespace sx


===== FILE: gl/upscale.cpp =====
// Video upscaling: FSR1 EASU+RCAS. See upscale.hpp.
//
// The FSR1 shaders are EVO Player's clean-room reimplementation (GPL-3.0),
// embedded via upscale_shaders.hpp. They use texelFetch directly — no
// textureGather, no CPU-side constants.

#include "upscale.hpp"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>

#include <GL/glcorearb.h>

#include "gfx/gl_program.hpp"
#include "upscale_shaders.hpp"
#include "util.h"

namespace {

void tex_params() {
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
}

}  // namespace

const char* VideoUpscaler::mode_name(UpscaleMode m) {
	switch (m) {
	case UpscaleMode::Fsr1: return "FSR1";
	case UpscaleMode::Fsr1Sharp: return "FSR1+RCAS";
	case UpscaleMode::Anime4k: return "Anime4K";
	default: return "";
	}
}

bool VideoUpscaler::gl_ok(const char* what) {
	GLenum e = glGetError();
	if (e != GL_NO_ERROR) {
		if (!logged_fail_) {
			logged_fail_ = true;
			dlog("upscale: %s: GL error 0x%x; upscaler disabled", what, unsigned(e));
		}
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

bool VideoUpscaler::ensure_fsr1() {
	if (easu_prog_) return true;
	auto fail = [&] {
		if (easu_prog_) glDeleteProgram(easu_prog_);
		if (rcas_prog_) glDeleteProgram(rcas_prog_);
		easu_prog_ = rcas_prog_ = 0;
		logged_fail_ = true;
		dlog("upscale: FSR1 shaders unavailable; upscaler disabled");
		return false;
	};
	easu_prog_ = hui::gfx::build_program("upscale_easu", kUpscaleVert, kUpscaleEasuFrag);
	if (!easu_prog_) return fail();
	rcas_prog_ = hui::gfx::build_program("upscale_rcas", kUpscaleVert, kUpscaleRcasFrag);
	if (!rcas_prog_) return fail();
	u_easu_src_ = glGetUniformLocation(easu_prog_, "u_src");
	u_rcas_src_ = glGetUniformLocation(rcas_prog_, "u_src");
	u_rcas_sharp_ = glGetUniformLocation(rcas_prog_, "u_sharp");
	if (u_easu_src_ < 0 || u_rcas_src_ < 0 || u_rcas_sharp_ < 0)
		return fail();
	glGenVertexArrays(1, &vao_);
	glGenFramebuffers(1, &fbo_);
	if (!gl_ok("upscale init")) return fail();
	dlog("upscale: FSR1 EASU+RCAS ready");
	return true;
}

bool VideoUpscaler::ensure() {
	if (easu_prog_) return true;
	if (logged_fail_) return false;
	return ensure_fsr1();
}

std::uint32_t VideoUpscaler::upscale(std::uint32_t src_tex, int src_w, int src_h,
                                               int dst_w, int dst_h, UpscaleMode mode, float sharpness,
                                               int& out_w, int& out_h) {
	if (!ready() || !src_tex || src_w <= 0 || src_h <= 0 || dst_w <= 0 || dst_h <= 0)
		return 0;
	if (mode != UpscaleMode::Fsr1 && mode != UpscaleMode::Fsr1Sharp)
		return 0;  // Anime4K not yet wired; caller falls back to bilinear
	if (!(src_w < dst_w && src_h < dst_h))
		return 0;  // nothing to upscale; caller draws directly

	// Working textures at display res. Both are always dst_w x dst_h; the size
	// is tracked once (tmp_w_/tmp_h_) and both are (re)allocated together.
	auto ensure_tex = [&](unsigned& tex) -> bool {
		if (tex) return true;
		glGenTextures(1, &tex);
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tex);
		glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA8, dst_w, dst_h, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, nullptr);
		tex_params();
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
		if (!gl_ok("upscale tex alloc")) {
			if (tex) glDeleteTextures(1, &tex);
			tex = 0;
			return false;
		}
		return true;
	};
	if (tmp_w_ != dst_w || tmp_h_ != dst_h) {
		if (tmp_tex_) { glDeleteTextures(1, &tmp_tex_); tmp_tex_ = 0; }
		if (out_tex_) { glDeleteTextures(1, &out_tex_); out_tex_ = 0; }
		tmp_w_ = dst_w;
		tmp_h_ = dst_h;
	}
	if (!ensure_tex(tmp_tex_)) return 0;
	// RCAS needs its own output texture (can't read+write the same one).
	if (mode == UpscaleMode::Fsr1Sharp && !ensure_tex(out_tex_)) return 0;

	GLint vp[4];
	glGetIntegerv(GL_VIEWPORT, vp);
	GLint prev_fbo = 0;
	glGetIntegerv(GL_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING, &prev_fbo);
	// hui's batch renderer leaves scissor/blend enabled; a fullscreen
	// triangle drawn under them gets clipped or composited against the
	// uninitialized working textures. Run the passes with a clean slate.
	GLboolean scissor = glIsEnabled(GL_SCISSOR_TEST);
	GLboolean blend = glIsEnabled(GL_BLEND);
	GLboolean depth = glIsEnabled(GL_DEPTH_TEST);
	glDisable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST);
	glDisable(GL_BLEND);
	glDisable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);
	glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, fbo_);
	glViewport(0, 0, dst_w, dst_h);

	auto draw_easu = [&]() -> bool {
		glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, tmp_tex_, 0);
		if (glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER) != GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE) {
			if (!logged_fail_) {
				logged_fail_ = true;
				dlog("upscale: framebuffer incomplete; upscaler disabled");
			}
			return false;
		}
		// EVO's EASU needs no CPU-side constants: it derives everything
		// from textureSize(u_src) and the vUV varying.
		glUseProgram(easu_prog_);
		glUniform1i(u_easu_src_, 0);
		glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0);
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, src_tex);
		glBindVertexArray(vao_);
		glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 3);
		glBindVertexArray(0);
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
		glUseProgram(0);
		return gl_ok("upscale easu");
	};

	auto draw_rcas = [&]() -> bool {
		glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, out_tex_, 0);
		if (glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER) != GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE) {
			if (!logged_fail_) {
				logged_fail_ = true;
				dlog("upscale: framebuffer incomplete; upscaler disabled");
			}
			return false;
		}
		glUseProgram(rcas_prog_);
		glUniform1i(u_rcas_src_, 0);
		glUniform1f(u_rcas_sharp_, sharpness);
		glActiveTexture(GL_TEXTURE0);
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, tmp_tex_);
		glBindVertexArray(vao_);
		glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 3);
		glBindVertexArray(0);
		glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
		glUseProgram(0);
		return gl_ok("upscale rcas");
	};

	bool ok = draw_easu();
	GLuint result = tmp_tex_;
	if (ok && mode == UpscaleMode::Fsr1Sharp) {
		ok = draw_rcas();
		result = out_tex_;
	}
	if (scissor) glEnable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST);
	if (blend) glEnable(GL_BLEND);
	if (depth) glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);
	glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, prev_fbo);
	glViewport(vp[0], vp[1], vp[2], vp[3]);
	if (!ok) return 0;
	out_w = dst_w;
	out_h = dst_h;
	return result;
}


===== FILE: gl/upscale.hpp =====
// Video upscaling: FSR1 (EASU+RCAS) and Anime4K for sub-display-resolution
// content. Replaces the bilinear stretch with edge-aware upscaling.
//
// Fail-closed by design, never required for correct playback:
//   - ensure() returns false when anything is unsupported; the caller keeps
//     the bilinear path.
//   - upscale() returns false on any GL failure; the caller draws the
//     source texture directly (bilinear) instead.
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

enum class UpscaleMode {
	Off = 0,
	Fsr1 = 1,        // EASU only
	Fsr1Sharp = 2,   // EASU + RCAS sharpening
	Anime4k = 3,     // Anime4K CNN x2 S (for anime content)
};

class VideoUpscaler {
public:
	VideoUpscaler() = default;
	~VideoUpscaler() = default;
	VideoUpscaler(const VideoUpscaler&) = delete;
	VideoUpscaler& operator=(const VideoUpscaler&) = delete;

	// Compile the shaders. Must be called with the GL context current
	// (the UI thread). False when the upscaler can't be used; logs once.
	bool ensure();
	bool ready() const { return easu_prog_ != 0; }

	// Upscale src_tex (src_w x src_h, RGBA8) to dst_w x dst_h.
	// Returns the upscaled texture on success (owned by the upscaler;
	// valid until the next upscale() call or a size change), 0 on any GL
	// failure (caller falls back to bilinear). out_w/out_h receive the
	// result size. sharpness is 0.0-1.0, used only for Fsr1Sharp.
	std::uint32_t upscale(std::uint32_t src_tex, int src_w, int src_h,
	                      int dst_w, int dst_h, UpscaleMode mode, float sharpness,
	                      int& out_w, int& out_h);

	// Human-readable name for stats-for-nerds. Empty when off/none.
	static const char* mode_name(UpscaleMode m);

private:
	bool ensure_fsr1();
	bool gl_ok(const char* what);

	unsigned easu_prog_ = 0, rcas_prog_ = 0;
	unsigned vao_ = 0, fbo_ = 0;
	// Working textures at display res: EASU renders into tmp_tex_,
	// RCAS reads tmp_tex_ and writes out_tex_ (no feedback loop).
	unsigned tmp_tex_ = 0, out_tex_ = 0;
	int tmp_w_ = 0, tmp_h_ = 0;
	// Uniform locations (EASU needs only the source texture; RCAS adds
	// a sharpness scalar).
	int u_easu_src_ = -1;
	int u_rcas_src_ = -1, u_rcas_sharp_ = -1;
	bool logged_fail_ = false;
};


===== FILE: gl/upscale_shaders.hpp =====
// Video upscaler shaders: FSR1 EASU + RCAS.
//
// Clean-room reimplementation by EVO Player (sainsaji/evo-player-ps5),
// GPL-3.0-or-later. Adapted from their AGC pipeline shaders to OpenGL:
//   - Vulkan `layout(set=N, binding=M)` replaced with plain uniforms
//   - `gl_VertexIndex` replaced with OpenGL `gl_VertexID`
//   - Vertex shader simplified (full-frame upscale needs no UV sub-rect)
//   - RCAS gains a `u_sharp` uniform for our adjustable sharpening slider
//     (EVO uses a fixed factor; u_sharp=1.0 reproduces their behavior)
//
// Source:
//   https://github.com/sainsaji/evo-player-ps5/blob/HEAD/projects/evoplayer/shaders/agc/upscale_easu.pipe
//   https://github.com/sainsaji/evo-player-ps5/blob/HEAD/projects/evoplayer/shaders/agc/upscale_rcas.pipe
//
#pragma once

// ==================== Fullscreen triangle ====================
static const char* kUpscaleVert = R"UPVERT(
layout(location = 0) out vec2 vUV;
void main() {
	vec2 p = vec2(float((gl_VertexID << 1) & 2), float(gl_VertexID & 2));
	vUV = p;
	gl_Position = vec4(p * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}
)UPVERT";

// ==================== FSR1 EASU ====================
// Edge-adaptive spatial upsampling. Input: source texture at native res.
// Output: display-sized framebuffer. vUV spans 0..1 across the output,
// which maps 1:1 onto the source (full-frame upscale).
static const char* kUpscaleEasuFrag = R"UPEASU(
uniform sampler2D u_src;
layout(location = 0) in vec2 vUV;
layout(location = 0) out vec4 out_color;

ivec2 g_sz;

vec3 S(ivec2 p) {
    return texelFetch(u_src, clamp(p, ivec2(0), g_sz - 1), 0).rgb;
}

/* FSR's cheap luma: B/2 + R/2 + G. */
float L(vec3 c) { return c.b * 0.5 + (c.r * 0.5 + c.g); }

/* Direction and length contribution of one of the four bilinear corners.
 * a = up, b = left, c = centre, d = right, e = down. */
void easu_set(inout vec2 dir, inout float len, float w,
              float a, float b, float c, float d, float e) {
    float dc = d - c;
    float cb = c - b;
    float lenX = max(abs(dc), abs(cb));
    lenX = 1.0 / max(lenX, 1.0 / 65536.0);
    float dirX = d - b;
    dir.x += dirX * w;
    lenX = clamp(abs(dirX) * lenX, 0.0, 1.0);
    len += lenX * lenX * w;

    float ec = e - c;
    float ca = c - a;
    float lenY = max(abs(ec), abs(ca));
    lenY = 1.0 / max(lenY, 1.0 / 65536.0);
    float dirY = e - a;
    dir.y += dirY * w;
    lenY = clamp(abs(dirY) * lenY, 0.0, 1.0);
    len += lenY * lenY * w;
}

/* Lanczos-2 approximation, stretched along the edge direction. */
void easu_tap(inout vec3 aC, inout float aW, vec2 off, vec2 dir, vec2 len,
              float lob, float clp, vec3 c) {
    vec2 v = vec2(off.x * dir.x + off.y * dir.y,
                  off.x * -dir.y + off.y * dir.x) * len;
    float d2 = min(v.x * v.x + v.y * v.y, clp);
    float wB = 0.4 * d2 - 1.0;
    float wA = lob * d2 - 1.0;
    wB *= wB;
    wA *= wA;
    wB = 1.5625 * wB - 0.5625;
    float w = wB * wA;
    aC += c * w;
    aW += w;
}

void main() {
    g_sz = textureSize(u_src, 0);
    vec2 pp = vUV * vec2(g_sz) - vec2(0.5);
    vec2 fp = floor(pp);
    pp -= fp;
    ivec2 o = ivec2(fp);

    /*      b c
     *    e f g h
     *    i j k l
     *      n o      f = o */
    vec3 bC = S(o + ivec2(0, -1)), cC = S(o + ivec2(1, -1));
    vec3 eC = S(o + ivec2(-1, 0)), fC = S(o),                gC = S(o + ivec2(1, 0)), hC = S(o + ivec2(2, 0));
    vec3 iC = S(o + ivec2(-1, 1)), jC = S(o + ivec2(0, 1)), kC = S(o + ivec2(1, 1)), lC = S(o + ivec2(2, 1));
    vec3 nC = S(o + ivec2(0, 2)),  oC = S(o + ivec2(1, 2));

    float bL = L(bC), cL = L(cC), eL = L(eC), fL = L(fC), gL = L(gC), hL = L(hC);
    float iL = L(iC), jL = L(jC), kL = L(kC), lL = L(lC), nL = L(nC), oL = L(oC);

    vec2 dir = vec2(0.0);
    float len = 0.0;
    easu_set(dir, len, (1.0 - pp.x) * (1.0 - pp.y), bL, eL, fL, gL, jL);
    easu_set(dir, len, pp.x * (1.0 - pp.y),         cL, fL, gL, hL, kL);
    easu_set(dir, len, (1.0 - pp.x) * pp.y,         fL, iL, jL, kL, nL);
    easu_set(dir, len, pp.x * pp.y,                 gL, jL, kL, lL, oL);

    vec2 dir2 = dir * dir;
    float dirR = dir2.x + dir2.y;
    bool zro = dirR < (1.0 / 32768.0);
    dirR = zro ? 1.0 : inversesqrt(dirR);
    dir.x = zro ? 1.0 : dir.x;
    dir *= vec2(dirR);

    len = len * 0.5;
    len *= len;
    float stretch = (dir.x * dir.x + dir.y * dir.y) / max(abs(dir.x), abs(dir.y));
    vec2 len2 = vec2(1.0 + (stretch - 1.0) * len, 1.0 - 0.5 * len);
    float lob = 0.5 + ((1.0 / 4.0 - 0.04) - 0.5) * len;
    float clp = 1.0 / lob;

    vec3 aC = vec3(0.0);
    float aW = 0.0;
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 0.0, -1.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, bC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 1.0, -1.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, cC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2(-1.0,  1.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, iC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 0.0,  1.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, jC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 0.0,  0.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, fC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2(-1.0,  0.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, eC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 1.0,  1.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, kC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 2.0,  1.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, lC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 2.0,  0.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, hC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 1.0,  0.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, gC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 1.0,  2.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, oC);
    easu_tap(aC, aW, vec2( 0.0,  2.0) - pp, dir, len2, lob, clp, nC);

    /* De-ring: clamp to the 2x2 neighbourhood. */
    vec3 mn = min(min(fC, gC), min(jC, kC));
    vec3 mx = max(max(fC, gC), max(jC, kC));
    vec3 pix = clamp(aC / max(aW, 1.0 / 65536.0), mn, mx);
    out_color = vec4(pix, 1.0);
}
)UPEASU";

// ==================== FSR1 RCAS ====================
// Robust contrast-adaptive sharpening. Input: EASU output (display-sized).
// Output: sharpened display-sized framebuffer. u_sharp 0.0-1.0 scales the
// sharpening lobe (1.0 = EVO's fixed strength).
static const char* kUpscaleRcasFrag = R"UPRCAS(
uniform sampler2D u_src;
uniform float u_sharp;
layout(location = 0) in vec2 vUV;
layout(location = 0) out vec4 out_color;

ivec2 g_sz;

vec3 S(ivec2 p) {
    return texelFetch(u_src, clamp(p, ivec2(0), g_sz - 1), 0).rgb;
}

float L(vec3 c) { return c.b * 0.5 + (c.r * 0.5 + c.g); }

void main() {
    g_sz = textureSize(u_src, 0);
    ivec2 ip = clamp(ivec2(vUV * vec2(g_sz)), ivec2(0), g_sz - 1);

    /*   b
     * d e f
     *   h   */
    vec3 b = S(ip + ivec2(0, -1));
    vec3 d = S(ip + ivec2(-1, 0));
    vec3 e = S(ip);
    vec3 f = S(ip + ivec2(1, 0));
    vec3 h = S(ip + ivec2(0, 1));

    float bL = L(b), dL = L(d), eL = L(e), fL = L(f), hL = L(h);

    /* Noise detection: back off on isolated single-pixel detail. */
    float nz = 0.25 * (bL + dL + fL + hL) - eL;
    float lmax = max(max(max(bL, dL), max(eL, fL)), hL);
    float lmin = min(min(min(bL, dL), min(eL, fL)), hL);
    nz = clamp(abs(nz) / max(lmax - lmin, 1.0 / 65536.0), 0.0, 1.0);
    nz = -0.5 * nz + 1.0;

    vec3 mn4 = min(min(b, d), min(f, h));
    vec3 mx4 = max(max(b, d), max(f, h));
    vec3 hitMin = min(mn4, e) / max(4.0 * mx4, vec3(1.0 / 65536.0));
    vec3 hitMax = (1.0 - max(mx4, e)) / min(4.0 * mn4 - 4.0, vec3(-1.0 / 65536.0));
    vec3 lobeRGB = max(-hitMin, hitMax);
    float lobe = max(-(0.25 - 1.0 / 16.0),
                     min(max(max(lobeRGB.r, lobeRGB.g), lobeRGB.b), 0.0)) * (0.8705506 * u_sharp);
    lobe *= nz;

    vec3 pix = (lobe * (b + d + f + h) + e) / (4.0 * lobe + 1.0);
    out_color = vec4(clamp(pix, 0.0, 1.0), 1.0);
}
)UPRCAS";


===== FILE: src/aniskip.cpp =====
#include "aniskip.h"

#include <chrono>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <thread>

#include "stremio.h"

namespace aniskip {

bool resolve_mal_id(const std::string& series_id, const std::string& title,
                    const std::atomic<bool>* cancel, int& mal_id,
                    bool* via_jikan) {
	mal_id = 0;
	if (via_jikan) *via_jikan = false;
	try {
		// Kitsu series ids look like "kitsu:12345": resolve through the
		// anime's external mappings to its MyAnimeList entry.
		// kitsu_answered tracks whether the Kitsu API responded at all: a
		// record with no MAL mapping must NOT fall back to the Jikan
		// popularity-sorted title search, which would attach some other
		// show's id. (review 2026-10-13)
		bool kitsu_answered = false;
		if (series_id.compare(0, 6, "kitsu:") == 0) {
			const std::string kid = series_id.substr(6);
			if (!kid.empty() && kid.find(':') == std::string::npos && kid.find('/') == std::string::npos) {
				json anime;
				std::string err;
				if (fetch_json("https://kitsu.app/api/edge/anime/" + kid, anime, err, 12, cancel)) {
					const json& rel = jobj(jobj(jobj(anime, "data"), "relationships"), "mappings");
					const std::string url = jstr(jobj(rel, "links"), "related");
					if (!url.empty() && url.compare(0, 8, "https://") == 0) {
						json mappings;
						if (fetch_json(url, mappings, err, 12, cancel)) {
							kitsu_answered = true;
							const json& arr = jobj(mappings, "data");
							if (arr.is_array()) {
								for (const auto& m : arr) {
									const json& a = jobj(m, "attributes");
									if (jstr(a, "externalSite") == "myanimelist/anime") {
										const int n = std::atoi(jstr(a, "externalId").c_str());
										if (n > 0) {
											mal_id = n;
											return true;
										}
									}
								}
							}
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		// Fallback (or non-Kitsu ids): Jikan title search, first hit.
		if (!kitsu_answered && !title.empty() && !(cancel && cancel->load())) {
			json res;
			std::string err;
			const std::string url =
			    "https://api.jikan.moe/v4/anime?q=" + url_encode(title) + "&limit=1&order_by=members&sort=desc";
			if (fetch_json(url, res, err, 12, cancel)) {
				const json& arr = jobj(res, "data");
				if (arr.is_array() && !arr.empty()) {
					const int n = static_cast<int>(jnum(arr.front(), "mal_id", 0));
					if (n > 0) {
						mal_id = n;
						// Jikan title search is a guess (popularity-sorted
						// first hit): flag it so the caller doesn't persist
						// a possibly-wrong id forever.
						if (via_jikan) *via_jikan = true;
						return true;
					}
				}
			}
		}
	} catch (...) {
		mal_id = 0;
	}
	return mal_id > 0;
}

bool fetch_skip_times(int mal_id, int episode, const std::atomic<bool>* cancel,
                      std::vector<SkipSegment>& out, bool* transport_failed) {
	out.clear();
	if (transport_failed) *transport_failed = false;
	if (mal_id <= 0 || episode <= 0) return false;
	for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 2; ++attempt) {
		if (attempt > 0) {
			// Retry once after 3s on transport failure (cancel-aware).
			for (int i = 0; i < 30; ++i) {
				if (cancel && cancel->load()) return false;
				std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100));
			}
			if (cancel && cancel->load()) return false;
		}
		try {
			char url[256];
			std::snprintf(url, sizeof(url),
			              "https://api.aniskip.com/v2/skip-times/%d/%d?types[]=op&types[]=ed&episodeLength=0",
			              mal_id, episode);
			json j;
			std::string err;
			if (!fetch_json(url, j, err, 12, cancel)) continue; // transport failure: retry
			if (!jbool(j, "found", false)) return false; // definitive: no data
			const json& results = jobj(j, "results");
			if (!results.is_array()) return false;
			for (const auto& r : results) {
				const std::string kind = jstr(r, "skipType");
				if (kind != "op" && kind != "ed") continue;
				const json& iv = jobj(r, "interval");
				const double start = jnum(iv, "startTime", -1);
				const double end = jnum(iv, "endTime", -1);
				if (start < 0 || end <= start) continue;
				SkipSegment s;
				s.start = start;
				s.end = end;
				s.kind = kind;
				out.push_back(s);
			}
			return !out.empty();
		} catch (...) {
			out.clear();
		}
	}
	// Both attempts died on transport (or were cancelled mid-retry).
	if (transport_failed) *transport_failed = true;
	return false;
}

std::string kind_label(const std::string& kind)
{
	if (kind == "ed") return "Outro";
	if (kind == "recap") return "Recap";
	if (kind == "credits") return "Credits";
	if (kind == "preview") return "Preview";
	return "Intro"; // "op", "intro", and anything unexpected
}

} // namespace aniskip

===== FILE: src/bidi.cpp =====
#include "bidi.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

#ifdef HAVE_FRIBIDI
#include <fribidi/fribidi.h>
#endif

namespace {

std::vector<uint32_t> utf8_decode(const std::string& s) {
	std::vector<uint32_t> out;
	for (size_t i = 0; i < s.size();) {
		unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i]);
		uint32_t cp;
		int n;
		if (c < 0x80) cp = c, n = 1;
		else if ((c >> 5) == 6) cp = c & 0x1f, n = 2;
		else if ((c >> 4) == 14) cp = c & 0x0f, n = 3;
		else if ((c >> 3) == 30) cp = c & 0x07, n = 4;
		else {
			i++;
			continue;
		}
		if (i + n > s.size()) break;
		for (int k = 1; k < n; k++) cp = (cp << 6) | (static_cast<unsigned char>(s[i + k]) & 0x3f);
		out.push_back(cp);
		i += size_t(n);
	}
	return out;
}

void utf8_put(std::string& out, uint32_t cp) {
	if (cp < 0x80) {
		out += char(cp);
	} else if (cp < 0x800) {
		out += char(0xc0 | (cp >> 6));
		out += char(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f));
	} else if (cp < 0x10000) {
		out += char(0xe0 | (cp >> 12));
		out += char(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f));
		out += char(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f));
	} else {
		out += char(0xf0 | (cp >> 18));
		out += char(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3f));
		out += char(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f));
		out += char(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f));
	}
}

bool is_rtl(uint32_t cp) {
	return (cp >= 0x0590 && cp <= 0x08ff) || (cp >= 0xfb1d && cp <= 0xfdff) || (cp >= 0xfe70 && cp <= 0xfeff);
}

// RML entities used by subtitles (subtitles.cpp) back to text, and the text
// escaped again afterwards.
std::string unescape(const std::string& s) {
	std::string out;
	for (size_t i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) {
		if (s[i] == '&') {
			size_t semi = s.find(';', i);
			if (semi != std::string::npos && semi - i <= 6) {
				std::string e = s.substr(i, semi - i + 1);
				const char* r = e == "&amp;"    ? "&"
				                : e == "&lt;"   ? "<"
				                : e == "&gt;"   ? ">"
				                : e == "&quot;" ? "\""
				                : e == "&apos;" ? "'"
				                : e == "&#39;"  ? "'"
				                : e == "&#123;" ? "{"
				                : e == "&#125;" ? "}"
				                                : nullptr;
				if (r) {
					out += r;
					i = semi;
					continue;
				}
			}
		}
		out += s[i];
	}
	return out;
}

std::string escape(const std::string& s) {
	std::string out;
	for (char c : s) {
		switch (c) {
		case '&': out += "&amp;"; break;
		case '<': out += "&lt;"; break;
		case '>': out += "&gt;"; break;
		case '{': out += "&#123;"; break;
		case '}': out += "&#125;"; break;
		default: out += c;
		}
	}
	return out;
}

}  // namespace

bool has_rtl(const std::string& utf8) {
	for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < utf8.size(); i++) {
		unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(utf8[i]);
		// U+0590..U+08FF start with 0xD6..0xE0; presentation forms with 0xEF 0xAC..0xBB.
		if ((c >= 0xd6 && c <= 0xdf) || (c == 0xe0 && static_cast<unsigned char>(utf8[i + 1]) <= 0xa3)) return true;
		if (c == 0xef && i + 1 < utf8.size()) {
			unsigned char d = static_cast<unsigned char>(utf8[i + 1]);
			if (d >= 0xac && d <= 0xbb) return true;
		}
	}
	return false;
}

std::string bidi_visual(const std::string& utf8) {
#ifdef HAVE_FRIBIDI
	if (!has_rtl(utf8)) return utf8;
	std::vector<uint32_t> in = utf8_decode(utf8);
	if (in.empty()) return utf8;
	std::vector<FriBidiChar> logical(in.begin(), in.end()), visual(in.size() + 1);
	FriBidiParType base = FRIBIDI_PAR_ON;  // from the text itself
	// log2vis: bidi reordering plus Arabic shaping (presentation forms,
	// lam-alef ligatures).
	if (!fribidi_log2vis(logical.data(), FriBidiStrIndex(logical.size()), &base, visual.data(), nullptr, nullptr,
	                     nullptr))
		return utf8;
	std::string out;
	for (size_t i = 0; i < logical.size(); i++) {
		uint32_t cp = visual[i];
		if (cp == 0xfeff || cp == 0x200c || cp == 0x200d || cp == 0x200e || cp == 0x200f) continue;  // invisible marks
		utf8_put(out, cp);
	}
	return out;
#else
	return utf8;
#endif
}

std::string bidi_visual_rml(const std::string& rml) {
	if (!has_rtl(rml)) return rml;
	std::string out;
	size_t start = 0;
	for (;;) {
		size_t br = rml.find("<br/>", start);
		std::string line = rml.substr(start, br == std::string::npos ? std::string::npos : br - start);
		if (has_rtl(line)) {
			// Text without its tags, reordered; italics/bold for the whole line.
			// The whole-cue color span is preserved too (the single-color rule
			// guarantees at most one).
			bool em = line.find("<em>") != std::string::npos, strong = line.find("<strong>") != std::string::npos;
			std::string color_open;
			size_t sp = line.find("<span");
			if (sp != std::string::npos) {
				size_t se = line.find('>', sp);
				if (se != std::string::npos) color_open = line.substr(sp, se - sp + 1);
			}
			std::string text;
			for (size_t i = 0; i < line.size(); i++) {
				if (line[i] == '<') {
					size_t end = line.find('>', i);
					if (end != std::string::npos) {
						i = end;
						continue;
					}
				}
				text += line[i];
			}
			line = escape(bidi_visual(unescape(text)));
			if (strong) line = "<strong>" + line + "</strong>";
			if (em) line = "<em>" + line + "</em>";
			if (!color_open.empty()) line = color_open + line + "</span>";
		}
		out += line;
		if (br == std::string::npos) break;
		out += "<br/>";
		start = br + 5;
	}
	return out;
}


===== FILE: src/bidi.h =====
// Right-to-left text (Arabic, Hebrew, ...) for the UI's text renderer, which
// lays glyphs out left to right and doesn't join Arabic letters itself: each
// line is reordered into display order and Arabic letters are replaced by
// their joined forms (Presentation Forms), with FriBidi. Without it, Arabic
// subtitles were missing glyphs (white boxes, issue #1) and, with a font,
// would have shown separate letters in reverse.
#pragma once

#include <string>

// True if the UTF-8 text has right-to-left letters.
bool has_rtl(const std::string& utf8);

// One line of plain UTF-8 text in display order, Arabic letters joined.
// Text without right-to-left letters comes back unchanged.
std::string bidi_visual(const std::string& utf8);

// The same for subtitle RML (escaped text, <em>/<strong>, <br/> between
// lines): each line with right-to-left letters is reordered; its inline
// tags are dropped, keeping italics/bold for the whole line.
std::string bidi_visual_rml(const std::string& rml);


===== FILE: src/hdr_probe.cpp =====
// One-time HDR10 signal probe, modeled on src/videoout_rate.cpp.
//
// Mechanism (hardware-verified in EVO Player's evo_agc_runtime.c, which this
// file's ABI mirrors): retype scanout buffers in place to HDR10
// (Bgr10A2Bt2100Pq, format 0x8100070400000000) with
// sceVideoOutSetBufferAttribute2 + sceVideoOutSubmitChangeBufferAttribute2,
// then read back sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus: dynamic_range == 2 means the TV
// entered HDR mode.
//
// Expected outcome on our build: the retype is refused / a no-op. Our EGL
// swapchain buffers are owned by the closed-source ps5-opengl driver, and
// this probe's fresh VideoOut handle has no buffer set registered on it, so
// there is nothing to retype. EVO documents (hardware 2026-09-28) that a
// refusal changes nothing, so this is a safe, useful negative result. A
// success (dynamic_range == 2) would mean Phase 2 HDR output is viable.
//
// Safety design (mirrors EVO's):
//  - Retype IN PLACE. Never unregister buffers: the on-screen set cannot be
//    unregistered (0x80290009 RESOURCE_BUSY) and the failed sequence once
//    blanked EVO's display.
//  - glFinish() first: no GPU write in the old format may land after a retype.
//  - Never mid-frame: this runs before the first frame is drawn.
//  - IMMEDIATE ROLLBACK to SDR on every path after the status readback.
//  - The VideoOut handle is opened per probe and closed before return; no
//    handle is held across frames, so EGL's display state is never disturbed.
//  - Symbols are resolved with dlsym by NAME (EVO: by-name works in the app
//    module; by raw NID fails). Missing symbols => SDR, logged.

#include "hdr_probe.h"

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>

#include <dlfcn.h>

#include <GLES2/gl2.h>  // glFinish: GPU idle before the retype

#include "util.h"  // dlog

namespace hdr_probe {
namespace {

// ABI per EVO's evo_agc_runtime.c (evo_vo_output_status).
struct OutputStatus
{
  uint32_t resolution;
  uint32_t dynamic_range;  // 0 unknown, 1 SDR, 2 HDR
  uint64_t refresh_rate;
  uint64_t flags;  // bit 0: HDR output active
  uint64_t reserved[3];
};

// Buffer attribute: 80 bytes, filled by sceVideoOutSetBufferAttribute2 from
// its parameters. The pixel format is a separate uint64_t argument, NOT a
// struct field (EVO: sceVideoOutSetBufferAttribute2(&attr, vfmt, 0, ...)).
struct BufferAttribute
{
  uint8_t bytes[80];
};

constexpr uint64_t kFormatSdr = UINT64_C(0x8000000000000000);    // Bgra8Srgb
constexpr uint64_t kFormatHdr10 = UINT64_C(0x8100070400000000);  // Bgr10A2Bt2100Pq

using OpenFn = int32_t (*)(int32_t user_id, int32_t type, int32_t index, const void *param);
using CloseFn = int32_t (*)(int32_t handle);
using GetStatusFn = int32_t (*)(int32_t handle, OutputStatus *status);
using SetAttrFn = void (*)(void *attribute, uint64_t format, uint32_t tiling,
                    uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint64_t option,
                    uint32_t reserved0, uint64_t reserved1);
using SubmitChangeFn = int32_t (*)(int32_t handle, int32_t set_index,
                                   const void *attribute, const void *option);

OpenFn g_open = nullptr;
CloseFn g_close = nullptr;
GetStatusFn g_get_status = nullptr;
SetAttrFn g_set_attr = nullptr;
SubmitChangeFn g_submit = nullptr;
bool g_resolved = false;

void resolve()
{
  if (g_resolved)
    return;
  g_resolved = true;
  g_open = reinterpret_cast<OpenFn>(dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "sceVideoOutOpen"));
  g_close = reinterpret_cast<CloseFn>(dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "sceVideoOutClose"));
  g_get_status =
    reinterpret_cast<GetStatusFn>(dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus"));
  g_set_attr =
    reinterpret_cast<SetAttrFn>(dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "sceVideoOutSetBufferAttribute2"));
  g_submit = reinterpret_cast<SubmitChangeFn>(
    dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "sceVideoOutSubmitChangeBufferAttribute2"));
  dlog("hdr_probe: dlsym open=%d close=%d getStatus=%d setAttr2=%d submitChange2=%d", !!g_open,
    !!g_close, !!g_get_status, !!g_set_attr, !!g_submit);
}

}  // namespace

void hdr_signal_probe(int width, int height)
{
  static bool done = false;  // one-time by construction; idempotent anyway
  if (done)
    return;
  done = true;

  dlog("hdr_probe: starting one-time HDR10 signal probe (%dx%d)", width, height);
  glFinish();  // GPU idle: no write in the old format after a retype

  resolve();
  if (!g_open || !g_close || !g_get_status || !g_set_attr || !g_submit)
  {
    dlog("hdr_probe: unavailable (symbols missing) - staying SDR");
    return;
  }

  // Per-operation handle (0xff/0/0, the pattern from the PS5 homebrew
  // samples and videoout_rate.cpp); closed before return on every path.
  const int32_t h = g_open(0xff, 0, 0, nullptr);
  if (h < 0)
  {
    dlog("hdr_probe: sceVideoOutOpen failed (%d) - staying SDR", h);
    return;
  }

  OutputStatus st{};
  int32_t rc = g_get_status(h, &st);
  dlog("hdr_probe: baseline GetOutputStatus rc=%d dynamic_range=%u (0 unknown, 1 SDR, 2 HDR)",
    rc, st.dynamic_range);

  // Retype the set in place to HDR10. set_index 0: our fresh handle has no
  // buffer set registered, so the expected result is a refusal (rc != 0),
  // which changes nothing.
  BufferAttribute attr{};
  g_set_attr(&attr, kFormatHdr10, 0, static_cast<uint32_t>(width),
      static_cast<uint32_t>(height), 0, 0, 0);
  rc = g_submit(h, 0, &attr, nullptr);
  dlog("hdr_probe: SubmitChangeBufferAttribute2(HDR10) rc=%d (0x%08x)", rc,
    static_cast<unsigned>(rc));
  if (rc != 0)
  {
    dlog("hdr_probe: display refused the HDR10 retype - unchanged, staying SDR");
    g_close(h);
    return;
  }

  memset(&st, 0, sizeof(st));
  rc = g_get_status(h, &st);
  dlog("hdr_probe: post-retype GetOutputStatus rc=%d dynamic_range=%u flags=0x%llx", rc,
    st.dynamic_range, static_cast<unsigned long long>(st.flags));
  if (st.dynamic_range == 2)
    dlog("hdr_probe: HDR SIGNAL DETECTED - TV entered HDR mode");
  else
    dlog("hdr_probe: no HDR signal (dynamic_range=%u) - Phase 2 not viable on this path",
        st.dynamic_range);

  // IMMEDIATE ROLLBACK to SDR on every path that got this far.
  memset(&attr, 0, sizeof(attr));
  g_set_attr(&attr, kFormatSdr, 0, static_cast<uint32_t>(width),
      static_cast<uint32_t>(height), 0, 0, 0);
  rc = g_submit(h, 0, &attr, nullptr);
  dlog("hdr_probe: rollback SubmitChangeBufferAttribute2(SDR) rc=%d (0x%08x)", rc,
    static_cast<unsigned>(rc));

  g_close(h);
  dlog("hdr_probe: done - display left in SDR");
}

}  // namespace hdr_probe


===== FILE: src/hdr_probe.h =====
#pragma once

// One-time HDR10 signal probe via libSceVideoOut (dlsym, never linked).
//
// Attempts EVO Player's HDR10 scanout-buffer retype
// (sceVideoOutSetBufferAttribute2 + sceVideoOutSubmitChangeBufferAttribute2
// with format 0x8100070400000000 = HDR10 Bgr10A2Bt2100Pq), checks whether the
// TV enters HDR mode via sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus, then IMMEDIATELY rolls
// back to SDR. Probe-only: no Settings UI, no rendering changes, HDR is
// never left enabled.
//
// Fails closed: any missing symbol, failed open, or refused call leaves the
// display exactly as it was and the app continues in SDR.
//
// Call once at startup, after EGL init, before the first frame (the screen
// is still black). Never call mid-frame. If a later eglSwapBuffers fails,
// the caller's existing swap-failure log covers it; this probe holds no
// VideoOut handle across frames.
namespace hdr_probe {

// width/height are the display dimensions, passed through to the buffer
// attribute like EVO does for its scanout.
void hdr_signal_probe(int width, int height);

}  // namespace hdr_probe


===== FILE: src/http.cpp =====
#include "http.h"

#include <curl/curl.h>

#include "util.h"

const char* kUserAgent = "Mozilla/5.0 (PlayStation; PlayStation 5/1.00) Stremio-PS5/1.0";

static std::string g_ca_bundle;

namespace {
// One curl easy handle per thread, kept across perform() calls. Reusing the
// handle reuses the underlying TCP/TLS connections and DNS results instead
// of paying a full handshake per request. curl_easy_reset() keeps the pooled
// connections alive while clearing every per-request option (URL, headers,
// timeouts, callbacks), all of which perform() sets again below. Handles are
// never shared between threads: thread_local gives each thread its own.
struct PooledCurl {
	CURL* c = nullptr;
	~PooledCurl() { if (c) curl_easy_cleanup(c); }
};

CURL* thread_curl() {
	thread_local PooledCurl pooled;
	if (!pooled.c) pooled.c = curl_easy_init();
	else curl_easy_reset(pooled.c);
	return pooled.c;
}
}  // namespace

std::string HttpResponse::describe() const {
	if (!error.empty()) return error;
	if (status == 0) return "no response";
	return "HTTP " + std::to_string(status);
}

void http_init(const std::string& ca_bundle_path) {
	curl_global_init(CURL_GLOBAL_ALL);
	g_ca_bundle = ca_bundle_path;
	dlog("curl %s, CA bundle %s (%s)", curl_version(), ca_bundle_path.c_str(),
	     file_exists(ca_bundle_path) ? "found" : "MISSING");
}

const std::string& http_ca_bundle() { return g_ca_bundle; }

#ifdef PLATFORM_PS5_NATIVE
extern "C" int console_curl_nonblocking(int socket);  // native/console_curl.c

static int on_socket(void*, curl_socket_t s, curlsocktype) {
	console_curl_nonblocking(s);  // without it a finished request can hang
	return CURL_SOCKOPT_OK;
}
#endif

void http_setup_handle(void* curl) {
#ifdef PLATFORM_PS5_NATIVE
	curl_easy_setopt(static_cast<CURL*>(curl), CURLOPT_SOCKOPTFUNCTION, on_socket);
#else
	(void)curl;
#endif
}

struct WriteState {
	std::string* out;
	std::size_t max_body;
};

static size_t write_cb(char* ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, void* userdata) {
	auto* st = static_cast<WriteState*>(userdata);
	st->out->append(ptr, size * nmemb);
	// Refuse absurd responses (a catalog or a poster is never this large).
	if (st->out->size() > st->max_body) return 0;
	return size * nmemb;
}

static int progress_cb(void* clientp, curl_off_t, curl_off_t, curl_off_t, curl_off_t) {
	auto* cancel = static_cast<const std::atomic<bool>*>(clientp);
	return (cancel && cancel->load()) ? 1 : 0;
}

static HttpResponse perform(const std::string& url, const std::string* post_body, long timeout_s,
                            const std::atomic<bool>* cancel, const std::vector<std::string>& headers,
                            std::size_t max_body) {
	HttpResponse r;
	CURL* c = thread_curl();  // pooled per thread; reset, options re-applied below
	if (!c) {
		r.error = "curl_easy_init failed";
		return r;
	}
	WriteState ws{&r.body, max_body};
	char errbuf[CURL_ERROR_SIZE] = {0};
	struct curl_slist* hdrs = nullptr;
	for (auto& h : headers) hdrs = curl_slist_append(hdrs, h.c_str());
	if (post_body) hdrs = curl_slist_append(hdrs, "Content-Type: application/json");

	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_URL, url.c_str());
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_USERAGENT, kUserAgent);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION, 1L);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_MAXREDIRS, 8L);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_ACCEPT_ENCODING, "");  // whatever curl was built with (gzip, br)
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, 10L);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_TIMEOUT, timeout_s);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_NOSIGNAL, 1L);
	// The PS5 has no IPv6 route; don't let an AAAA record fail the connect.
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_IPRESOLVE, CURL_IPRESOLVE_V4);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_ERRORBUFFER, errbuf);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION, write_cb);
	curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_WRITEDATA, &ws);
	if (!g_ca_bundle.empty() && file_exists(g_ca_bundle)) curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_CAINFO, g_ca_bundle.c_str());
	http_setup_handle(c);
	if (cancel) {
		curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_NOPROGRESS, 0L);
		curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION, progress_cb);
		curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_XFERINFODATA, (void*)cancel);
	}
	if (hdrs) curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, hdrs);
	if (post_body) {
		curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_POST, 1L);
		curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, post_body->c_str());
		curl_easy_setopt(c, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDSIZE, long(post_body->size()));
	}

	CURLcode rc = curl_easy_perform(c);
	if (rc != CURLE_OK) {
		r.error = errbuf[0] ? errbuf : curl_easy_strerror(rc);
		if (cancel && cancel->load()) r.error = "cancelled";
		char* ip = nullptr;
		curl_easy_getinfo(c, CURLINFO_PRIMARY_IP, &ip);
		dlog("http: %s %s -> %s (ip %s)", post_body ? "POST" : "GET", log_url(url).c_str(), r.error.c_str(),
		     ip && *ip ? ip : "none");
	}
	curl_easy_getinfo(c, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE, &r.status);
	char* ct = nullptr;
	if (curl_easy_getinfo(c, CURLINFO_CONTENT_TYPE, &ct) == CURLE_OK && ct) r.content_type = ct;
	if (hdrs) curl_slist_free_all(hdrs);
	// No curl_easy_cleanup: the handle stays pooled for the next request.
	return r;
}

HttpResponse http_get(const std::string& url, long timeout_s, const std::atomic<bool>* cancel,
                      const std::vector<std::string>& headers, std::size_t max_body) {
	return perform(url, nullptr, timeout_s, cancel, headers, max_body);
}

HttpResponse http_post_json(const std::string& url, const std::string& body, long timeout_s,
                            const std::atomic<bool>* cancel) {
	return perform(url, &body, timeout_s, cancel, {}, 64u * 1024 * 1024);
}

namespace {

const uint16_t kSysmoduleVideodec2 = 207;
const uint32_t kCodecAvc = 1, kCodecHevc = 974921, kCodecVp9 = 2382845;
const uint32_t kResourceCompute = 1;
const size_t kInputSlotBytes = 8u << 20;  // ~50x the largest 4K keyframe seen
const unsigned kInputSlots = 4;
const unsigned kFrameSlots = 8;
const int kReorderDepth = 4;
const int kReorderSlots = kReorderDepth + 1;
const int kPtsPool = kReorderDepth + int(kInputSlots) + 8;
const int kPostFlushErrors = 32;  // refusals tolerated before the first picture after a seek
const int kMaxW = 3840, kMaxH = 2176;

bool g_module_loaded = false;

enum Kind { H264, HEVC, VP9, HEVC10, KIND_COUNT };

struct CodecDesc {
	Kind kind;
	uint32_t codec_type, profile;
	int level_1080, level_4k;
	const char* bsf;
	bool vp9;
	const char* tag;
	unsigned depth;
};

// max_level: AVC level x10, HEVC general_level_idc (x30), VP9 x10.
const CodecDesc kCodecs[KIND_COUNT] = {
    {H264, kCodecAvc, 100, 51, 52, "h264_mp4toannexb", false, "H.264", 4},
    {HEVC, kCodecHevc, 1, 123, 153, "hevc_mp4toannexb", false, "HEVC", 4},
    {VP9, kCodecVp9, 0, 41, 51, "vp9_superframe_split", true, "VP9", 4},
    {HEVC10, kCodecHevc, 2, 123, 153, "hevc_mp4toannexb", false, "HEVC 10-bit", 4},
};

size_t align16k(size_t v) { return (v + 0x3fffu) & ~size_t(0x3fff); }

int alloc_direct(size_t size, int prot, int64_t* start, void** addr) {
	int rc = sceKernelAllocateDirectMemory(0, sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize(), size, 0x4000, 12, start);
	if (rc == 0) rc = sceKernelMapDirectMemory(addr, size, prot, 0, *start, 0x4000);
	return rc;
}
void free_direct(void* addr, int64_t start, size_t size) {
	if (addr) sceKernelMunmap(addr, size);
	if (start >= 0) sceKernelReleaseDirectMemory(start, size);
}

// One decoder per codec, kept for the next video of the same kind (creating
// one maps a few hundred MB; doing that per video would fragment memory).
struct Slot {
	bool ready = false, owned = false;
	void* compute_queue = nullptr;
	void* compute_mem = nullptr;
	int64_t compute_start = -1;
	size_t compute_size = 0;
	void* decoder = nullptr;
	void* cpu_mem = nullptr;
	size_t cpu_map = 0;
	bool cpu_direct = false;  // workspace in direct memory (flexible memory was short)
	int64_t cpu_start = -1;
	void* gpu_mem = nullptr;
	int64_t gpu_start = -1;
	size_t gpu_size = 0;
	void* cpu_gpu_mem = nullptr;
	int64_t cpu_gpu_start = -1;
	size_t cpu_gpu_size = 0;
	void* input_mem = nullptr;
	int64_t input_start = -1;
	size_t input_pool = 0;
	void* frame_mem = nullptr;
	int64_t frame_start = -1;
	size_t frame_pool = 0, frame_size = 0;
	int max_w = 0, max_h = 0;
	SceVideodec2DecoderConfigInfo cfg{};
	SceVideodec2DecoderMemoryInfo mem{};
};

std::mutex g_slots_m;
Slot g_slots[KIND_COUNT];

void slot_teardown(Slot& s) {
	if (s.decoder) sceVideodec2DeleteDecoder(s.decoder);
	free_direct(s.frame_mem, s.frame_start, s.frame_pool);
	free_direct(s.input_mem, s.input_start, s.input_pool);
	free_direct(s.cpu_gpu_mem, s.cpu_gpu_start, s.cpu_gpu_size);
	free_direct(s.gpu_mem, s.gpu_start, s.gpu_size);
	if (s.cpu_mem) {
		if (s.cpu_direct) {
			free_direct(s.cpu_mem, s.cpu_start, s.cpu_map);
		} else {
			sceKernelReleaseFlexibleMemory(s.cpu_mem, s.cpu_map);
			sceKernelMunmap(s.cpu_mem, s.cpu_map);
		}
	}
	if (s.compute_queue) sceVideodec2ReleaseComputeQueue(s.compute_queue);
	free_direct(s.compute_mem, s.compute_start, s.compute_size);
	s = Slot();
}

// Sony calls can fault instead of failing: each step is logged before it
// runs, so the last line in the log names the one that did.
#define STAGE(name)                                                    \
	do {                                                               \
		stage = (name);                                                \
		dlog("hwdec: %s %dx%d [%s]", d.tag, w, h, stage);              \
	} while (0)

int slot_bringup(Slot& s, const CodecDesc& d, int w, int h) {
	const char* stage = "?";
	int rc;
	SceVideodec2ComputeMemoryInfo cm{};
	SceVideodec2ComputeConfigInfo cc{};
	cm.size = sizeof cm;
	STAGE("QueryComputeMemoryInfo");
	if ((rc = sceVideodec2QueryComputeMemoryInfo(&cm)) != 0) goto fail;
	s.compute_size = align16k(size_t(cm.cpu_gpu_size));
	STAGE("alloc(compute)");
	if ((rc = alloc_direct(s.compute_size, 0x33, &s.compute_start, &s.compute_mem)) != 0) goto fail;
	cm.cpu_gpu = s.compute_mem;
	cm.cpu_gpu_size = s.compute_size;
	cc.size = sizeof cc;
	STAGE("AllocateComputeQueue");
	if ((rc = sceVideodec2AllocateComputeQueue(&cc, &cm, &s.compute_queue)) != 0) goto fail;
	if (!s.compute_queue) {
		rc = -1;
		goto fail;
	}
	{
		SceVideodec2DecoderConfigInfo config{};
		SceVideodec2DecoderMemoryInfo mem{};
		config.size = sizeof config;
		config.resource_type = kResourceCompute;
		config.codec_type = d.codec_type;
		config.profile = d.profile;
		config.max_level = uint32_t((w > 1920 || h > 1088) ? d.level_4k : d.level_1080);
		config.max_width = w;
		config.max_height = h;
		config.max_dpb_frames = -1;  // the decoder sizes it
		config.pipeline_depth = d.depth;
		config.compute_queue = uint64_t(s.compute_queue);
		config.cpu_affinity = 0x3f;
		config.cpu_priority = 700;
		config.optimize_progressive = 1;
		mem.size = sizeof mem;
		STAGE("QueryDecoderMemoryInfo");
		if ((rc = sceVideodec2QueryDecoderMemoryInfo(&config, &mem)) != 0) goto fail;
		{
			int64_t st = 0;
			size_t avail = 0;
			sceKernelAvailableDirectMemorySize(0, sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize(), 0x4000, &st, &avail);
			dlog("hwdec: needs workspace %llu KB, gpu %llu KB, cpu_gpu %llu KB, frames %u x %llu KB, input %zu KB; "
			     "%zu MB direct memory free",
			     (unsigned long long)(mem.cpu_size >> 10), (unsigned long long)(mem.gpu_size >> 10),
			     (unsigned long long)(mem.cpu_gpu_size >> 10), kFrameSlots,
			     (unsigned long long)(mem.max_frame_size >> 10), (kInputSlotBytes * kInputSlots) >> 10, avail >> 20);
		}

		// The decoder's CPU workspace: flexible memory, as the decoder
		// expects. This app has little of it, so if that fails, try
		// direct memory mapped for the CPU.
		s.cpu_map = align16k(size_t(mem.cpu_size));
		size_t flex = 0;
		sceKernelAvailableFlexibleMemorySize(&flex);
		STAGE("MapNamedFlexibleMemory");
		rc = sceKernelMapNamedFlexibleMemory(&mem.cpu, s.cpu_map, 0x03, 0, "StremioVdec");
		if (rc != 0 || !mem.cpu) {
			dlog("hwdec: workspace of %zu KB not in flexible memory (rc 0x%08x, %zu KB free); using direct memory",
			     s.cpu_map >> 10, unsigned(rc), flex >> 10);
			mem.cpu = nullptr;
			STAGE("alloc(workspace)");
			if ((rc = alloc_direct(s.cpu_map, 0x33, &s.cpu_start, &mem.cpu)) != 0) goto fail;
			s.cpu_direct = true;
		}
		s.cpu_mem = mem.cpu;

		s.gpu_size = align16k(size_t(mem.gpu_size));
		s.cpu_gpu_size = align16k(size_t(mem.cpu_gpu_size));
		s.frame_size = align16k(size_t(mem.max_frame_size));
		s.input_pool = kInputSlotBytes * kInputSlots;
		s.frame_pool = s.frame_size * kFrameSlots;
		if (!s.frame_size) {
			rc = -1;
			goto fail;
		}
		mem.gpu_size = s.gpu_size;
		if (s.cpu_gpu_size) mem.cpu_gpu_size = s.cpu_gpu_size;
		STAGE("alloc(gpu)");
		if ((rc = alloc_direct(s.gpu_size, 0x33, &s.gpu_start, &s.gpu_mem)) != 0) goto fail;
		mem.gpu = s.gpu_mem;
		if (s.cpu_gpu_size) {
			STAGE("alloc(cpu_gpu)");
			if ((rc = alloc_direct(s.cpu_gpu_size, 0x33, &s.cpu_gpu_start, &s.cpu_gpu_mem)) != 0) goto fail;
			mem.cpu_gpu = s.cpu_gpu_mem;
		}
		STAGE("alloc(input)");
		if ((rc = alloc_direct(s.input_pool, 0x33, &s.input_start, &s.input_mem)) != 0) goto fail;
		STAGE("alloc(frames)");
		if ((rc = alloc_direct(s.frame_pool, 0x33, &s.frame_start, &s.frame_mem)) != 0) goto fail;
		STAGE("CreateDecoder");
		if ((rc = sceVideodec2CreateDecoder(&config, &mem, &s.decoder)) != 0 || !s.decoder) {
			if (!rc) rc = -1;
			goto fail;
		}
		s.cfg = config;
		s.mem = mem;
		STAGE("Reset");
		if ((rc = sceVideodec2Reset(s.decoder)) != 0) goto fail;
		s.max_w = w;
		s.max_h = h;
		s.ready = true;
		dlog("hwdec: %s decoder ready for %dx%d (%zu MB)", d.tag, w, h,
		     (s.compute_size + s.gpu_size + s.cpu_gpu_size + s.input_pool + s.frame_pool + s.cpu_map) >> 20);
		return 0;
	}
fail:
	dlog("hwdec: %s %dx%d failed at [%s]: rc 0x%08x", d.tag, w, h, stage, unsigned(rc));
	slot_teardown(s);
	return rc ? rc : -1;
}
#undef STAGE

// A new decoder object on the slot's memory: what a seek needs. Reset alone
// left some 4K streams unable to restart (Nuvio PS5, hardware 2026-10-01).
int slot_renew(Slot& s) {
	if (s.decoder) sceVideodec2DeleteDecoder(s.decoder);
	s.decoder = nullptr;
	SceVideodec2DecoderMemoryInfo mem = s.mem;
	int rc = sceVideodec2CreateDecoder(&s.cfg, &mem, &s.decoder);
	if (rc != 0 || !s.decoder) {
		s.decoder = nullptr;
		return rc ? rc : -1;
	}
	return sceVideodec2Reset(s.decoder);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// HEVC access-unit handling

const int kNalTrailHi = 5, kNalRaslN = 8, kNalRaslR = 9, kNalIrapHi = 23;

// First VCL NAL type in an Annex-B access unit, or -1.
int hevc_au_nal_type(const uint8_t* au, int size) {
	for (int i = 0; i + 4 < size; i++) {
		if (au[i] != 0 || au[i + 1] != 0) continue;
		int payload;
		if (au[i + 2] == 1) payload = i + 3;
		else if (au[i + 2] == 0 && au[i + 3] == 1) payload = i + 4;
		else continue;
		if (payload >= size) break;
		int type = (au[payload] >> 1) & 0x3f;
		if (type <= kNalIrapHi) return type;
		i = payload;
	}
	return -1;
}

struct Bits {
	const uint8_t* p;
	int n, byte, bit, zeros;
	int get() {
		if (byte >= n) return 0;
		if (bit == 0 && zeros >= 2 && p[byte] == 3) {  // emulation prevention
			byte++;
			zeros = 0;
			if (byte >= n) return 0;
		}
		int v = (p[byte] >> (7 - bit)) & 1;
		if (++bit == 8) {
			zeros = p[byte] == 0 ? zeros + 1 : 0;
			bit = 0;
			byte++;
		}
		return v;
	}
	unsigned u(int k) {
		unsigned v = 0;
		while (k-- > 0) v = (v << 1) | unsigned(get());
		return v;
	}
	unsigned ue() {
		int lz = 0;
		while (lz < 31 && !get()) lz++;
		return ((1u << lz) - 1) + u(lz);
	}
};

// The ID a VPS (32), SPS (33) or PPS (34) defines.
unsigned hevc_ps_id(int type, const uint8_t* payload, int len) {
	Bits b{payload, len, 0, 0, 0};
	if (type == 32) return b.u(4);
	if (type == 34) return b.ue();
	b.u(4);
	unsigned subs = b.u(3);
	b.u(1);
	b.u(32), b.u(32), b.u(32);
	unsigned prof[8] = {0}, lvl[8] = {0};
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < subs && i < 8; i++) prof[i] = b.u(1), lvl[i] = b.u(1);
	if (subs > 0)
		for (unsigned i = subs; i < 8; i++) b.u(2);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < subs && i < 8; i++) {
		if (prof[i]) b.u(32), b.u(32), b.u(24);
		if (lvl[i]) b.u(8);
	}
	return b.ue();
}

// Copies an HEVC access unit without what the decoder can't take: NAL types
// 48-63 (Dolby Vision RPU / enhancement layer; the base layer plays) and a
// parameter set that a later one in the same AU replaces (UHD Blu-ray remuxes
// repeat theirs in-band; two different PPS 0 in one AU make the decoder
// refuse the keyframe).
int hevc_copy_base_layer(uint8_t* dst, const uint8_t* au, int size) {
	const int kMaxNals = 512;
	static thread_local int sc_at[kMaxNals], nal_at[kMaxNals], end_at[kMaxNals];
	static thread_local uint32_t key[kMaxNals];
	int count = 0, sc = -1, nal = -1;
	for (int i = 0; i + 3 <= size; i++)
		if (au[i] == 0 && au[i + 1] == 0 && au[i + 2] == 1) {
			sc = (i > 0 && au[i - 1] == 0) ? i - 1 : i;
			nal = i + 3;
			break;
		}
	if (nal < 0) {
		memcpy(dst, au, size_t(size));
		return size;
	}
	while (nal < size && count < kMaxNals) {
		int next_sc = size, next_nal = -1;
		for (int j = nal; j + 3 <= size; j++)
			if (au[j] == 0 && au[j + 1] == 0 && au[j + 2] == 1) {
				next_sc = (j > nal && au[j - 1] == 0) ? j - 1 : j;
				next_nal = j + 3;
				break;
			}
		int type = (au[nal] >> 1) & 0x3f;
		sc_at[count] = sc;
		nal_at[count] = nal;
		end_at[count] = next_sc;
		key[count] = 0;
		if (type >= 32 && type <= 34 && nal + 2 < next_sc) {
			unsigned layer = ((au[nal] & 1u) << 5) | (au[nal + 1] >> 3);
			unsigned id = hevc_ps_id(type, au + nal + 2, next_sc - nal - 2);
			key[count] = 0x80000000u | (uint32_t(type) << 24) | (layer << 16) | (id & 0xffffu);
		}
		count++;
		if (next_nal < 0) break;
		sc = next_sc;
		nal = next_nal;
	}
	if (count == kMaxNals && nal < size) {
		memcpy(dst, au, size_t(size));
		return size;
	}
	int o = 0;
	for (int k = 0; k < count; k++) {
		int type = (au[nal_at[k]] >> 1) & 0x3f;
		if (type >= 48) continue;
		if (key[k]) {
			bool replaced = false;
			for (int m = k + 1; m < count && !replaced; m++) replaced = key[m] == key[k];
			if (replaced) continue;
		}
		memcpy(dst + o, au + sc_at[k], size_t(end_at[k] - sc_at[k]));
		o += end_at[k] - sc_at[k];
	}
	return o;
}

// tiles_enabled_flag of an HEVC PPS: the hardware decoder doesn't do tiles.
bool hevc_pps_tiles(const uint8_t* payload, int len) {
	Bits b{payload, len, 0, 0, 0};
	b.ue(), b.ue();
	b.u(1), b.u(1);
	b.u(3);
	b.u(1), b.u(1);
	b.ue(), b.ue();
	b.ue();
	b.u(1), b.u(1);
	if (b.u(1)) b.ue();
	b.ue(), b.ue();
	b.u(1), b.u(1), b.u(1);
	b.u(1);
	return b.u(1) != 0;
}

bool hevc_extradata_tiles(const uint8_t* x, int n) {
	if (!x || n < 4) return false;
	if (x[0] == 0 && x[1] == 0 && (x[2] == 1 || (x[2] == 0 && x[3] == 1))) {
		for (int i = 0; i + 4 < n; i++) {
			if (x[i] || x[i + 1] || x[i + 2] != 1) continue;
			int nal = i + 3;
			if (((x[nal] >> 1) & 0x3f) == 34 && hevc_pps_tiles(x + nal + 2, n - nal - 2)) return true;
		}
		return false;
	}
	if (n < 23) return false;
	int pos = 23, arrays = x[22];
	for (int a = 0; a < arrays && pos + 3 <= n; a++) {
		int type = x[pos] & 0x3f;
		int count = (x[pos + 1] << 8) | x[pos + 2];
		pos += 3;
		for (int k = 0; k < count && pos + 2 <= n; k++) {
			int len = (x[pos] << 8) | x[pos + 1];
			pos += 2;
			if (pos + len > n) return false;
			if (type == 34 && len > 2 && hevc_pps_tiles(x + pos + 2, len - 2)) return true;
			pos += len;
		}
	}
	return false;
}

// H.264 SPS (RBSP, NAL header already skipped): num_reorder_frames from the
// VUI bitstream-restriction info. -1 when absent or unparseable.
int h264_sps_num_reorder_frames(const uint8_t* rbsp, int len) {
	Bits b{rbsp, len, 0, 0, 0};
	unsigned profile = b.u(8);
	b.u(8);  // constraint flags
	b.u(8);  // level_idc
	b.ue();  // seq_parameter_set_id
	if (profile == 100 || profile == 110 || profile == 122 || profile == 244 || profile == 44 ||
	    profile == 83 || profile == 86 || profile == 118 || profile == 128 || profile == 138 ||
	    profile == 139 || profile == 134 || profile == 135) {
		if (b.ue() == 3) b.u(1);  // chroma_format_idc, separate_colour_plane_flag
		b.ue();                   // bit_depth_luma_minus8
		b.ue();                   // bit_depth_chroma_minus8
		b.u(1);                   // qpprime_y_zero_transform_bypass_flag
		if (b.u(1)) return -1;    // scaling lists: not worth the skip logic
	}
	b.ue();  // log2_max_frame_num_minus4
	unsigned poc = b.ue();
	if (poc == 0) b.ue();
	else if (poc == 1) {
		b.u(1);
		b.ue();
		b.ue();  // se() values skipped as ue(): identical bit length
		unsigned n = b.ue();
		if (n > 32) return -1;
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; i++) b.ue();
	}
	b.ue();  // max_num_ref_frames
	b.u(1);  // gaps_in_frame_num_value_allowed_flag
	b.ue();
	b.ue();  // pic_width/height_in_mbs_minus1
	if (!b.u(1)) b.u(1);  // frame_mbs_only_flag / mb_adaptive_frame_field_flag
	b.u(1);              // direct_8x8_inference_flag
	if (b.u(1)) {
		b.ue();
		b.ue();
		b.ue();
		b.ue();  // frame crop offsets
	}
	if (!b.u(1)) return -1;  // no VUI: num_reorder_frames lives there
	if (b.u(1)) {            // aspect_ratio_info_present_flag
		if (b.u(8) == 255) {
			b.u(16);
			b.u(16);
		}
	}
	if (b.u(1)) b.u(1);  // overscan_info_present_flag
	if (b.u(1)) {        // video_signal_type_present_flag
		b.u(3);
		b.u(1);
		b.u(1);
		if (b.u(1)) {
			b.u(8);
			b.u(8);
			b.u(8);  // colour description
		}
	}
	if (b.u(1)) {
		b.ue();
		b.ue();  // chroma_sample_loc_type_top/bottom_field
	}
	if (b.u(1)) {
		b.u(32);
		b.u(32);
		b.u(1);  // timing info
	}
	bool nal_hrd = b.u(1), vcl_hrd = b.u(1);
	if (nal_hrd || vcl_hrd) {
		// Skip hrd_parameters() (once or twice): only the bit positions matter.
		for (int h = 0, hn = (nal_hrd && vcl_hrd) ? 2 : 1; h < hn; h++) {
			unsigned cpb = b.ue();
			if (cpb > 31) return -1;
			b.u(4);
			b.u(4);
			for (unsigned i = 0; i <= cpb; i++) {
				b.ue();
				b.ue();
				b.u(1);
			}
			b.u(5);
			b.u(5);
			b.u(5);
			b.u(5);
		}
		b.u(1);  // low_delay_hrd_flag
	}
	b.u(1);  // pic_struct_present_flag
	if (!b.u(1)) return -1;  // bitstream_restriction_flag
	b.u(1);                 // motion_vectors_over_pic_boundaries_flag
	b.ue();
	b.ue();
	b.ue();
	b.ue();
	unsigned reorder = b.ue();  // num_reorder_frames
	if (b.byte > b.n) return -1;
	return int(reorder);
}

// HEVC SPS (RBSP, 2-byte NAL header already skipped): the largest
// sps_max_num_reorder_pics over the sub-layers. -1 when absent/unparseable.
int hevc_sps_max_num_reorder_pics(const uint8_t* rbsp, int len) {
	Bits b{rbsp, len, 0, 0, 0};
	b.u(4);  // sps_video_parameter_set_id
	unsigned max_sub = b.u(3);
	if (max_sub > 6) return -1;
	b.u(1);  // sps_temporal_id_nesting_flag
	// profile_tier_level(profilePresentFlag=1, maxNumSubLayersMinus1):
	b.u(2);
	b.u(1);
	b.u(5);  // general_profile_space/tier/idc
	b.u(32);  // general_profile_compatibility_flag[32]
	b.u(1);
	b.u(1);
	b.u(1);
	b.u(1);  // progressive/interlaced/non_packed/frame_only
	b.u(44);  // general_reserved_zero_44bits
	b.u(8);   // general_level_idc
	bool sub_prof[8] = {false}, sub_lvl[8] = {false};
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < max_sub; i++) {
		sub_prof[i] = b.u(1) != 0;
		sub_lvl[i] = b.u(1) != 0;
	}
	if (max_sub > 0)
		for (unsigned i = max_sub; i < 8; i++) b.u(2);  // reserved_zero_2bits
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < max_sub; i++) {
		if (sub_prof[i]) {
			b.u(2);
			b.u(1);
			b.u(5);
			b.u(32);
			b.u(1);
			b.u(1);
			b.u(1);
			b.u(1);
			b.u(44);  // sub-layer profile fields (no level_idc here)
		}
		if (sub_lvl[i]) b.u(8);  // sub_layer_level_idc[i]
	}
	b.ue();  // sps_seq_parameter_set_id
	if (b.ue() == 3) b.u(1);  // chroma_format_idc == 3: separate_colour_plane_flag
	b.ue();
	b.ue();  // pic_width/height_in_luma_samples
	if (b.u(1)) {
		b.ue();
		b.ue();
		b.ue();
		b.ue();  // conformance window offsets
	}
	b.ue();
	b.ue();  // bit_depth_luma/chroma_minus8
	b.ue();  // log2_max_pic_order_cnt_lsb_minus4
	bool ordering_info = b.u(1) != 0;  // sps_sub_layer_ordering_info_present_flag
	unsigned start = ordering_info ? 0 : max_sub;
	int reorder = -1;
	for (unsigned i = start; i <= max_sub; i++) {
		b.ue();  // sps_max_dec_pic_buffering_minus1[i]
		int r = int(b.ue());  // sps_max_num_reorder_pics[i]
		if (r > reorder) reorder = r;
		b.ue();  // sps_max_latency_increase_plus1[i]
	}
	if (b.byte > b.n) return -1;
	return reorder;
}

// First SPS NAL out of an avcC (ISO BMFF) H.264 extradata block.
bool avcc_first_sps(const uint8_t* x, int n, const uint8_t*& rbsp, int& len) {
	if (!x || n < 7 || x[0] != 1) return false;
	int num = x[5] & 0x1f, pos = 6;
	for (int i = 0; i < num && pos + 2 <= n; i++) {
		int l = (x[pos] << 8) | x[pos + 1];
		pos += 2;
		if (l < 2 || pos + l > n) return false;
		if ((x[pos] & 0x1f) == 7) {  // SPS NAL type
			rbsp = x + pos + 1;  // skip the 1-byte NAL header
			len = l - 1;
			return true;
		}
		pos += l;
	}
	return false;
}

// First SPS NAL out of an hvcC (ISO BMFF) HEVC extradata block.
bool hvcc_first_sps(const uint8_t* x, int n, const uint8_t*& rbsp, int& len) {
	if (!x || n < 23 || x[0] != 1) return false;
	int pos = 23, arrays = x[22];
	for (int a = 0; a < arrays && pos + 3 <= n; a++) {
		int type = x[pos] & 0x3f, count = (x[pos + 1] << 8) | x[pos + 2];
		pos += 3;
